376: Built around Arco-Flagellants, Mortifiers, and Zephyrim delivered by Palatine and Canoness character stacks, Penitent Host throws waves of frenzied close-combat units into the mid-board at speed. The engine is attrition-through-volume: Arco-Flagellants and Mortifiers exploit their high attack counts and Deadly Demise triggers to trade up into expensive units while Zephyrim use their fly movement and Heroic Intervention access to protect flanks and deny opponent scoring lanes. It punishes slow durable-grind lists and static gunlines that lack the activation density to clear multiple simultaneous multi-wound melee threats before they connect. It cracks open against concentrated anti-infantry firepower — Blast templates and massed AP-2 volume from Heavy Gunline or Transport Infantry lists strip the low-toughness Penitent chassis faster than the Canoness aura stack can regenerate pressure, leaving the army unable to replace lost melee reach.
288: Built around Skitarii Marshals pushing Sicarian Ruststalkers and Infiltrators forward alongside Pteraxii Skystalkers and Ironstrider Ballistarii, the Skitarii Hunter Cohort is AdMech's mixed-profile skirmish list — a T3-5 toolbox of fast infantry and walking vehicles that punches well above its fragile-looking stat line. The engine is board-wide pressure: Pteraxii deepstrike onto mid-table objectives while Sicarians and Rangers grind the scoring zones and Ballistarii provide mobile AP-2 overwatch, cycling Doctrinas each turn to re-spec the army's damage profile against whatever needs answering. It punishes static gunlines and low-activation vehicle armies by flooding objectives with distinct unit types before the opponent can concentrate fire — the activation gap is the real weapon. What cracks it open is any list running massed AP-3+ or Lethal Hits at range, since T3 Skitarii with no native invulnerable save evaporate under sustained quality shooting before the Sicarian counter-charge can connect.
310: Warlock Skyrunners, Warlock Conclave, Windriders, and War Walkers form the core of a psyker-saturated Aeldari battlegroup that layers jetbike mobility over a dense buff-character network. The plan is to stack Preternatural Precision's Lethal Hits and Sustained Hits 1 triggers onto War Walkers and Windrider fire platforms each turn while the Conclave's psychic support shifts the army's damage profile to match whatever target the opponent presents, grinding primary through mobile objective-holding across multiple flanks. Against static shooting armies and mid-T infantry hordes the combination of 4+ invuln from Warlock auras, high-movement repositioning, and Lethal Hits volume is punishing — it out-trades anything that can't catch it or crack layered defenses efficiently. The build folds against concentrated AP-3+ anti-armour fire that targets the relatively fragile T4-5 jetbike chassis before the buff stack is assembled, and losing key Warlock characters early collapses the entire psychic engine.
375: Built around Celestian Sacresants with Hospitaller support, Junith Eruita leading the melee wedge, and Saint Celestine as a hammer-and-resurrect engine, this is the Hallowed Martyrs melee host — an Immolator-delivered elite combat list wearing a surprisingly fast, mobile skin. The plan is to deliver Sacresants into mid-board engagements early, cycle Hospitaller revivals and Celestine resurrections to sustain bodies on objectives across multiple turns, and outscore opponents through attrition-resistant primary holding rather than raw damage output. It punishes lists that can't efficiently clear 4+ invuln melee blobs — particularly static gunlines and infantry hordes that lack dedicated anti-elite tools, where layered Feel No Pain equivalents and Celestine's guaranteed return make piecemeal clearance impossible. It cracks open against fast skimmer fire and mobile anti-armour at range, where Raider or Wave Serpent kiting and AP-3+ volume can pick apart the Immolator delivery chassis before Sacresants ever reach engagement range.
366: Built around Custodian Wardens and Blade Champions as the melee hammers, Caladius Grav-Tanks for mobile fire support, and Allarus Custodians as deep-striking shock troops, with Witchseekers providing the allied Sisters of Silence screen that makes this a Lions of the Emperor list rather than a generic Shield Host. The plan is to advance the Caladius chassis into mid-board firing positions while the 2+/4++ infantry claims and holds objectives, using Allarus deep-strike threats to punish opponents who over-extend trying to contest. Against static gunlines and durable infantry the 2+/4++ across every Custodian model trivialises return fire while Blade Champion Precision attacks strip key characters before the main grind begins. The list struggles against concentrated AP-3+ Melta from mobile platforms — Mont'ka Crisis Suits and Chaos Knight Infernal Lance builds can spike through the ion-shield-equivalent saves before the Caladius can reposition, and the low activation count means a single bad turn of anti-tank focus fire removes the mobile-fire component entirely.
286: Built around Skorpius Disintegrators, Sicarian Ruststalkers and Infiltrators, Skitarii Rangers, and Servitor Battleclade formations, Haloscreed Battle Clade runs a dense mixed-profile AdMech roster where T4-5 Sicarian elites and Ranger blobs screen fast vehicle fire from Disintegrator and Ironstrider platforms. The engine is sustained mid-board pressure — Ruststalkers deliver Lethal Hits melee into exposed units while Infiltrators strip ObSec from contested objectives, and Disintegrators provide S7 AP-1 volume fire that punishes anything that tries to push back; the list scores primary by simply being harder to clear than it looks. It punishes static heavy gunlines and transport-delivered hammer units that commit into the mid-board and find their target priority split between durable T5 Sicarians, hull-point-soaking Skorpius chassis, and Ranger blobs that refuse to leave objectives. It cracks open against concentrated AP-3+ anti-armour and fast skimmer kiting, because the Disintegrators are the anti-infantry spine and individually fragile, and the list has no answer for a mobile army that avoids the engagement entirely.
367: Built around Venerable Land Raiders ferrying Custodian Guard with Prosecutors and Witchseekers riding alongside, this is Lions of the Emperor — the transport-delivered melee brick with a Sisters of Silence and Inquisitor support shell bolted on. It scores by disgorging 2+/4++ Custodian Guard onto mid-board objectives from Land Raider hulls that themselves demand dedicated anti-tank attention, while Witchseeker Psycannons and Inquisitor Draxus suppress psychic threats and chip screening units before the door drops. The 2+/4++ layered defense stack punishes any list that can't concentrate AP-3+ or Melta volume — mobile melee toolboxes, infantry hordes, and skimmer-fire lists all bounce off Custodians that simply refuse to die to sub-AP-3 output. Concentrated Melta or Knight-chassis Avenger Gatling fire cracks it open by killing the Land Raiders before disembarkation, leaving expensive Custodian units stranded in the open without transport protection or threat range.
309: Built around Troupes delivered in Starweavers, a Troupe Master stacking combat buffs, Skyweavers on the flanks, and a Solitaire as the assassination piece, this is a Harlequin-dominant Aeldari shell that reads like Reaper's Wager without the Drukhari backbone. The plan is to fire-and-fade Starweavers into mid-board each turn — disgorging Troupes to spike a priority target with volume Lethal Hits via Preternatural Precision, then pulling the chassis back behind cover while Skyweavers contest secondaries the opponent can't reach. It punishes static gunlines and slow durable-grind lists that can't catch 14"-move skimmer transports or pin down a Solitaire hunting characters, and the 4+ invuln on Skyweavers plus the Harlequin melee profile means Russ-company fire bounces inefficiently off the delivery screen. However, the list's fragility collapses against concentrated AP-3+ anti-vehicle shooting — one round of focused Melta or Avenger Gatling fire strips the Starweavers and leaves Troupes stranded on foot, where their 6+ armor makes them extremely vulnerable to any subsequent shooting.
369: Built around Vertus Praetors and a Shield-Captain on Dawneagle Jetbike, this is a Custodes jetbike cavalry list running a fast, multi-threat roster supported by Allarus Custodians, Trajann Valoris, and a Blade Champion as melee hammer options — the Talons of the Emperor skimmer expression without the Sisters of Silence scaffold. It wins by using 14" jetbike movement with Assault-keyword shooting to dictate engagement range turn by turn, farming primary through superior board coverage while the 2+/4++ saves on every model absorb far more return fire than the low model count suggests. Against Heavy Gunline Toolbox lists, the jetbike speed denies firing arcs entirely — Russ Demolishers and static fire bases can't track 14"-move platforms that reposition every shooting phase, and the 4+ invuln shrugs off blast-template chip damage that would clear conventional skimmer chassis. The list cracks under concentrated Mobile Anti-Armour pressure: Knight-class melta at AP-3+ and T'au Mont'ka railfire can consistently punch through 2+/4++ at volume, and the low activation count means the jetbike list can't spread the threat wide enough to deny focus fire on its most expensive pieces.
287: Built around Cybernetica Datasmith-buffed Kastelan Robots supported by Onager Dunecrawlers, Kataphron Breachers, and Skitarii Vanguard screens, this is the Haloscreed Battle Clade's robot-brick expression — a slow, T6-7 mid-board grind that leans on Repulsor Grid's shooting-reflect and Phosphor Blasters for volume output. The plan is to plant Kastelans on contested objectives turn 1, flip them into Aegis protocols when the opponent commits, and dare the enemy to trade into a 5++ invuln plus Feel No Pain stack while Onagers and Breachers clean up whatever survives the robot wall. It punishes mid-range shooting lists and mobile toolbox deepstrike plays that can't efficiently crack T6 with 5++ saves across multiple activations before falling behind on primary. However, concentrated AP-3+ anti-armour fire — Knight Demolishers, Melta from Mont'ka Battlesuits, Dark Reapers with Lethal Hits — bypasses the invuln math entirely, and the list's near-zero mobility means it cannot recover once outmaneuvered on secondaries, a chronic problem reflected in its tournament results.
308: Built around Swooping Hawks, Warp Spiders, Dark Reapers, Howling Banshees, and Fire Dragons cycling through Wave Serpents, Aspect Host deploys the full aspect-warrior roster as a multi-tool that re-specs its damage profile every turn via Preternatural Precision — spending Shrine Tokens to stack Lethal Hits plus Sustained Hits 1 on whichever unit needs to punch above its weight class that activation. The engine scores through relentless repositioning and secondary farming: Warp Spiders and Swooping Hawks steal Behind Enemy Lines and Engage on All Fronts while Dark Reapers with Lethal Hits delete the key unit that would contest an objective, keeping primary climbing without ever planting a static anchor. It punishes mid-board brawlers and horde armies that can't match its AP-2/AP-3 Lethal Hits volume, and the Banshee Mask 4+ invuln plus Forceshield stacking means T5-6 mob attacks largely bounce. At sub-50% win rate the list's fragility is the tell — concentrated AP-3 Melta from Knights or Mont'ka Crisis Suits strips Wave Serpents before the aspect cargo deploys, and without transports the foot aspects are too slow and too lightly armoured to recover the primary gap.
374: Built around Castigators, Immolators, Retributors, Dominions, and Seraphim, this is a fast mechanised Sisters list that plays more like a Drukhari raiding party than a static gunline — fire-on-the-move Assault weapons on mobile chassis backed by multi-melta Retributors as the anti-armour anchor. The engine is dictating engagement range: Immolators advance-and-fire their Heavy Flamers or Multi-Meltas into priority targets while Seraphim apply Pistol pressure and Castigators hammer anything mid-to-heavy armour that survives, scoring primary through tempo rather than attrition. Against planted Heavy Gunline lists and slow grind armies, the combination of 14"-move transports, Assault-keyword weapons, and Retributor Melta spikes punishes anything that can't reposition or hide behind LoS blockers. Fast melee toolbox lists and Mobile Anti-Armour threats — particularly anything with 4+ invulns closing the gap or matched vehicle speed with AP-3+ Melta — crack the list open by stripping the fragile transport chassis before the Sisters can dictate the trade.
311: Built around Fire Prisms, Corsair Skyreavers, Corsair Voidreavers, and Prince Yriel in a Windrider Host-adjacent shell, this is a fast armoured-vehicle list that punishes static armies from range while Corsair skirmishers contest primaries in the midfield. The engine is Fire Prism laser-link stacking — two or more Prisms combining fire for a single high-AP Strength 9 shot that bypasses invulnerable saves, backed by Corsair harassment units claiming objectives the opponent can't safely contest without walking into the firing solution. Shroud Runners and War Walkers screen the Prisms and exploit secondary angles while Prince Yriel's aura buffs push the Lethal Hits threshold across multiple activations, making the list disproportionately dangerous against elite low-model-count armies with 3+ saves and T5-7 chassis. The list cracks when faced with fast mobile anti-armour — Knight chassis or Mont'ka Crisis Suits matching the Fire Prisms' movement speed while concentrating AP-3+ Melta into the T7 vehicle hull that the entire scoring engine depends on, stripping the list of both its firepower and its ability to contest midfield.
319: Built around Militarum Tempestus Command Squads, Tempestus Scions, Kasrkin, and Krieg Combat Engineers delivered via Chimeras, Bridgehead Strike is the elite-infantry-in-transports variant of Guard — not a tank company, not a Conscript blob, but a precision strike force that punches well above its model count. It scores by deep-striking or mechanised-advancing Scions and Kasrkin onto midfield objectives early, using Nork Deddog and command auras to keep elite squads alive long enough to hold, while Chimeras provide mobile fire support and redeployment flexibility. The transport-delivery structure punishes slow positional armies — Mass Volume Horde and planted gunlines can't contest objectives fast enough once Scion squads drop in and claim them with volume fire and high OC. What cracks it open is concentrated anti-transport firepower: any list that can reliably pop Chimeras turn 1 — Knights with Avenger Gatlings, CSM with Dark Pact ranged contracts — strips the delivery mechanism and leaves expensive infantry squads stranded on foot in the open.
368: Built around three or more Dreadnought variants — Venerable Contemptor, Telemon, and Contemptor-Achillus — supported by Caladius Grav-Tanks and Anathema Psykana Rhino screening, this is Solar Spearhead at its most machine-heavy: an elite vehicle brick with virtually no infantry beyond what's needed to screen and deliver buffs. It wins by parking 2+/4++ T9-10 chassis on mid-board objectives and daring the opponent to spend their entire damage budget cracking them open, while the Achillus and Galatus variants punish anything that closes to melee. It punishes static gunlines and mass-infantry hordes hardest — Blast templates and anti-infantry firepower waste themselves on a five-model list, and the Telemon's Caestus-and-Spiculus volume combined with Caladius lance fire creates an AP-3+ anti-armour answer that most shooty-castle lists can't match for sustained damage efficiency. Concentrated Melta at range cracks it open: Mont'ka Crisis Battlesuits and Infernal Lance Despoilers can strip hull points faster than the 4++ absorbs, and with minimal activations the list bleeds primary scoring the moment one vehicle is isolated and deleted.
345: Built around Crusader Squads in large blobs, Assault Intercessors, High Marshal Helbrecht, and Chaplain Grimaldus delivering zealot buffs across a dense infantry line, this is a Righteous Crusaders list that floods the board with high-OC bodies rather than relying on a single hammer unit. The engine is primary-score dominance through sheer body count — Helbrecht's re-roll aura and Grimaldus's litanies keep the blobs punching above their weight in melee while the list grinds out objective control across all five markers. It punishes static gunlines and transport-mech lists that can't generate enough activation volume to clear 20-30-model Crusader blobs supported by a Lieutenant's re-rolls and sticky-objective pressure. It cracks open against concentrated blast-template firepower and fast kiting lists — Russ Demolishers and Wave Serpents alike can either delete blobs wholesale or deny the engagement entirely, leaving Helbrecht with nothing profitable to charge into.
346: Righteous Crusaders built around Bladeguard Veterans anchored by a Judiciar, Sword Brethren as the secondary strike package, and an Execrator providing mobile fire support, with Infiltrators screening forward and a Techmarine keeping the chassis honest. The plan is to use the Judiciar's Temporal Snap to deny enemy Fight Phase reactions while Bladeguard and Sword Brethren push into mid-board objectives, relying on 4+ invuln saves and 3+ armor to absorb the alpha strike before the melee trade resolves in your favor. This build punishes opposing lists that need the Fight Phase to function — anything relying on pile-in sequencing, Heroic Intervention, or Fight on Death triggers gets shut down by the Judiciar, and the Bladeguard's 4+ invuln holds against AP-2 chip shooting that would strip other elite infantry. The 39% win rate reveals the core weakness plainly: without meaningful ranged threat, fast skimmer lists kite the whole formation indefinitely, and any list that can clear the Judiciar early through Precision shooting leaves the Bladeguard exposed to the exact counter-punch they were built to prevent.
344: Built around a Castellan and Marshal leading Sword Brethren and Assault Intercessors delivered in Impulsors, with a Repulsor Executioner anchoring the backfield, this is a Gladius Task Force list that grafts Black Templars' crusading melee identity onto a hybrid mech-gunline chassis. The Repulsor Executioner's Macro-cannon and twin Heavy Onslaught Gatling array handle heavy lifting at range while Impulsors push Sword Brethren into mid-board, with the Castellan's Rites of Battle stacking hit rerolls across both modes to keep the damage output consistent. It punishes slow, durable lists that can't contest the mid-board — planted gunlines and horde blobs get shot apart by the Repulsor before the Sword Brethren's AP-2 attacks close the deal. Fast skimmer and deepstrike lists crack it open by targeting the Impulsors before they disgorge their cargo, stranding elite infantry in the open without the transport-delivery engine that makes the scoring plan work.
322:
Built around Death Korps of Krieg blobs, Krieg Combat Engineers, and Death Riders, this is a Recon Element or Combined Regiment infantry castle with a distinctly Krieg character — massed T3 bodies in 20-man squads, Ursula Creed and Cadian Castellan stacking Orders, and Death Riders providing the only real threat of proactive engagement.

The plan is raw OC saturation: flood three or four objectives with 40-60 Krieg infantry by turn 2, use Creed's Order economy to double down on key squads, and grind primary scoring while Combat Engineers and Death Riders threaten flanking units trying to contest. The win condition is simply having more bodies on more objectives across turns 3-5 than the opponent can clear.

This list punishes Transport Infantry and Mid-T Brawler matchups where activation count and wound pool decide the primary race — a Pactbound Rhino-rush or War Horde mob can't out-OC 60 Krieg models when Creed is handing out Take Aim! orders to two squads per turn.

The 45% win rate signals a hard weakness against Heavy Gunline and Mobile Anti-Armour matchups: Russ Demolisher Blast templates delete 8-12 T3 Krieg per activation, and Knight Avenger Gatlings ignore the wound pool entirely — T3 with no invuln and no FNP simply collapses under concentrated AP-2+ volume before it can establish the
321: Built around Rogal Dorn Battle Tanks and Leman Russ Vanquishers anchoring the fire line, with Lord Solar Leontus commanding Attilan Rough Riders, Taurox-delivered Gaunt's Ghosts, and supporting infantry for objective coverage, this is Grizzled Company's mobile-gunline variant — a planted heavy-weapon platform that leans harder into anti-armour reach than the pure Russ tank company. The plan is to delete high-value targets with the Dorn's S14 AP-3 Armoured Fist Cannons and Vanquisher Battle Cannons at range, use Leontus to vector Rough Riders into exposed flanks, and let Gaunt's Ghosts precision-screen or harass characters while the tank line accrues primary from a static second-row position. It punishes mid-range brawlers and Transport Infantry hard — the Dorn's volume of AP-3+ fire pops Rhinos on turn one and the Vanquisher cracks anything that emerges, while Rough Rider lances intercept counter-charges before they reach the tanks. It cracks badly against fast skimmer lists and Mobile Toolbox deepstrike threats, because the planted firing line has no answers to fire-and-fade Raiders staying outside arc or Skorpekh squads teleporting directly into the tank formation on turn one.
298: Built around Vindicators as a demolisher-fire backbone paired with The Sanguinor, Sanguinary Guard, and a jump-pack Captain, this is a Liberator Assault Group hybrid that leans on blast-template pressure to clear midfield while elite jump infantry finish what the cannons start. The Vindicators' S14 AP-3 Demolisher Siege Cannon forces opponents off objectives or punishes clumped bodies, while Sanguinary Guard and the Sanguinor crash in behind the smoke to convert damage into primary scoring. It punishes static gunlines and T7-9 vehicle lists that can't reposition away from Demolisher arcs and can't trade efficiently into 4+ invuln jump infantry closing at speed. It cracks open against fast kiting lists — skimmer-mech and mobile toolbox threats that stay at 24"+ and chip the slow-moving Vindicators with anti-tank fire before the jump infantry can close the engagement distance.
299: Built around Bladeguard Veterans and Sanguinary Priests riding Impulsors forward alongside Assault Intercessors led by a Blood Angels Captain and Lieutenant, this is the Liberator Assault Group's signature Impulsor-rush melee delivery package. The engine is turn-2 disembarkation: Impulsors drive 12" turn one while the Captain and Priest stack full re-rolls and FNP onto the Bladeguard, who then pile out with a Death Company-style charge to isolate and delete a priority target while Assault Intercessors claim the vacated objective. The 4++ on Bladeguard combined with Sanguinary Priest's FNP means the brick survives light return fire and keeps scoring primary, punishing slower gunlines that can't concentrate enough AP-2+ shots to clear it in one activation. What cracks this open is concentrated AP-3 anti-elite shooting before the Impulsors reach melee range — anything with massed Melta or Demolisher-cannon fire strips the transports turn one and forces the hammers to walk into withering fire before they can swing.
297: Built around Death Company Dreadnoughts, jump-pack Death Company Marines driven by Lemartes, and Sanguinary Guard as the elite finisher layer, this is the Liberator Assault Group expression of Blood Angels at its most aggression-forward — a multi-wave melee delivery engine with Scout squads holding the rear. The plan is to saturate the mid-board with fast, hard-to-clear threats simultaneously: Lemartes amplifies Death Company charge output while the Dreadnought anchors the kill zone, forcing the opponent to split fire across several high-priority units or lose the trade on whichever they ignore. It punishes static gunlines and low-activation vehicle lists that can't clear multiple T6-plus, FNP-stacked jump threats in a single turn, especially when the Dreadnought's fight-on-death profile taxes any unit that does commit. Concentration of AP-2-or-better anti-elite shooting — particularly anything that can strip the Dreadnought and Sanguinary Guard in the same turn — cracks the engine before it closes distance, and any list with deep board presence or layered screens can delay the charge window long enough to outscore it on primary.
325: Built around Bloodletters in large blobs, Bloodcrushers as the elite shock cavalry, Flesh Hounds as the fast screen-and-flank threat, and a Rendmaster on Blood Throne stacking Khorne aura buffs, this is a Blood Legion melee-tide anchored by a Bloodthirster hammer. The win condition is multi-wave engagement: Flesh Hounds pressure screens on turn 1 while Bloodcrushers and the Bloodthirster funnel the opponent into a reactive posture, letting Bloodletter blobs pile onto contested objectives and generate primary through sheer OC volume backed by sticky-threat denial. Its strength is punishing Mid-T Brawler and Mass Volume Horde lists — Lethal Hits from Khorne weapon profiles sidestep T5-6 toughness math, and the layered threat vectors mean no single defensive position survives all three waves. It cracks against Mobile Anti-Armour and planted Heavy Gunline lists, where AP-3+ Melta and Blast templates evaporate Bloodletter blobs before they close, and the army's near-zero shooting weight means it can't threaten chassis it can't reach in melee.
320: Built around Scout Sentinels, Hellhounds, Leman Russ Exterminators and Battle Tanks, a Rogal Dorn Commander, and Tech-Priest Enginseer support, this is a Grizzled Company tank column leaning hard into mixed-chassis firepower across every range band. The plan is to plant Russes and the Dorn in firing-line positions turn one, use Hellhounds and Sentinels as fast chaff-clearers and objective-grabbers, and grind primary scoring while the tank battery deletes whatever the opponent presents — Exterminators scything infantry with twin autocannons, the Dorn Commander soaking return fire with its 2+ save and T11 chassis. It punishes static gunlines and infantry hordes most efficiently: Exterminator autocannons and Hellhound Inferno Cannons clear blobs that would tarpit most lists, while the Dorn's AP-2 Battle Cannon volume makes light-vehicle screens irrelevant. Fast mobile threats with concentrated anti-armour — Knights, Mont'ka Battlesuits, or deepstriking melee hammers — crack it open by closing range before the firing line can reposition, exploiting the near-zero mobility of the Russ battery.
318: Built around Bullgryns as a melee anvil, Catachan Jungle Fighters as a resilient infantry base, Kasrkin as an elite strike element, and Rogal Dorn Commander tanks as the heavy-weapon backbone, this is Grizzled Company playing a hybrid armoured-infantry role rather than pure Russ spam. Ruthless Discipline's doubled Order economy supercharges the Rogal Dorn platforms and Chimera-delivered Kasrkin, letting the list dictate range while Bullgryns wall off midfield objectives that the Catachan blobs then sticky. It punishes Transport Infantry and Mid-T Brawler lists hard — the combination of Blast templates clearing screens, Bullgryn T6 2+ blocking counter-charges, and Commissar-anchored Battle Shock immunity means neither Rhino-rush nor mob-advance gets traction before the scoring gap opens. Mobile anti-armour lists and deep-striking melee toolboxes crack it, however, since the Chimeras and Dorns are priority targets that, once popped, strand the Kasrkin on foot and expose the Bullgryn wall to concentrated AP-3+ focus fire before it can lock engagement.
323: Beasts of Nurgle, Flesh Hounds, Skarbrand, and a Great Unclean One form the core of this Daemonic Incursion build — a mixed-god attrition engine where Nurgle's sticky, regenerating bodies anchor objectives while Khorne's fast melee threats close distance and Be'lakor provides utility through Shadows of Chaos. The list scores by planting Plaguebearers and Beasts of Nurgle on objectives under multiple defensive layers — FNP-equivalent Disgustingly Resilient, high wound pools, and Lethal Hits triggers on Nurgle weapons — while Flesh Hounds and Skarbrand threaten elimination of isolated damage dealers that overcommit trying to clear the blob. It punishes static gunlines and transport-infantry lists that need to grind through 30+ wounds of T5-6 bodies per objective, trading shooting efficiency for a primary-scoring race they simply can't win against this volume of sticky OC. Fast, high-AP vehicle lists exposing Melta at close range are the crack: Beasts of Nurgle and Plaguebearers have no native invuln save, so concentrated AP-3+ Melta or Knight Despoiler fire can delete anchor units faster than the regeneration cycle replaces them.
296: Built around Sanguinary Guard, Death Company Marines with Jump Packs, and Assault Intercessors with Jump Packs led by a Captain with Jump Pack, this is the Liberator Assault Group in its most aggressive expression — a jump-pack-delivered melee hammer backed by a Gladiator Lancer firing line and Scout screens holding home objectives. The engine is a coordinated multi-wave air assault: Scout screens deny deepstrike denial and hold primaries while the jump pack units commit into mid-board, using high-movement threat projection and the Captain's re-roll auras to spike damage on isolated targets before the Lancer's S14 AP-3 Damage D6 cleans up survivors at range. It punishes static gunlines and transport-infantry lists that can't react to simultaneous threats at multiple ranges — the Lancer handles vehicle priority targets while the jump pack elites tie up or eliminate scoring infantry before they can contest. The list struggles against layered-defense and heavy-invuln builds like Custodes Talons or Death Guard Vectorium, where AP-3 Lethal Hits are load-bearing and the jump pack units' melee volume fails to punch through 2+/4++ or Disgustingly Resilient FNP efficiently enough to clear objectives before the grind-engine takes over.
324: Built around Screamers, Flamers, and a Lord of Change or Kairos Fateweaver as the psychic-and-daemon-aura spine, this is Tzeentch's answer to the all-comers roster — a fast, invuln-stacked toolbox that hits the board from multiple angles simultaneously. The engine is tempo-driven objective control backed by Pink Horror split-spawning to maintain body count mid-table, while Screamers' Bladevane slashing and Flamers' Warpflame volume (Lethal Hits on the crit roll) delete isolated targets the Lord of Change or Be'lakor has isolated with debuffs. Its 4+/5++ invulnerable layering across nearly every datasheet punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox lists whose Blast templates and AP-2 shooting waste potential against daemon saves, and the sheer activation count from Horror reinforcement cycles grinds out primary against low-model-count shooting armies. Fast melee that can bypass the psychic screen — specifically Mark of Khorne Transport Infantry with counter-punch screening — and volume-fire Mobile Toolbox brawlers that ignore the invuln math by stacking enough raw attacks will crack it, as neither the Lord of Change nor Be'lakor survives sustained concentrated melee pressure once their screening chaff is tabled.
326: Built around Great Unclean One, Poxbringer, Sloppity Bilepiper, and bloated mobs of Plaguebearers and Beasts of Nurgle, this is Plague Legion at its most suffocating — a Nurgle daemon tide that plays more like Virulent Vectorium than classic Chaos Daemons. The engine is attrition scoring: Plaguebearers sticky-hold objectives through Disgustingly Resilient-equivalent layering and sheer wound pool, while the Great Unclean One and Beasts of Nurgle deliver Lethal Hits melee pressure that forces inefficient trades from anything trying to clear the blob. It punishes static gunlines and low-activation vehicle lists hardest, since neither can generate enough output per turn to clear T5 Plaguebearer mobs stacked with FNP-equivalent saves before the primary score runs away. Fast, fragile delivery lists and dedicated mobile anti-armour are the killers — anything with AP-3+ Melta or fire-and-fade movement tempo can either delete the Great Unclean One before it engages or kite the entire army off primary indefinitely.
340: Built around War Dog Brigands as the core anti-armour platform — backed by Huntsmen, Karnivores, a Knight Desecrator, and a Nurglings screen — this is an Infernal Lance list leaning hard into Wardog spam rather than TITANIC anchor play. The engine is volume-of-chassis: Brigands combine indirect-fire Havoc Missiles with Daemonbreath Spears to delete key targets from outside LoS on turn 1, while Karnivores close the distance to lock surviving threats in melee before they can reposition. It punishes slow durable-grind lists — Death Guard Vectorium and Custodes Talons specifically — where the combination of AP-3+ Melta range, indirect Blast coverage, and Hammer of Wrath triggers cracks T7-9 chassis and 2+/4++ bricks that melee-only lists can't efficiently trade into. The glaring weakness is activation count: at 6-9 chassis total, mob-tarpits from War Horde Orks or Pactbound Cultist screens absorb the punch and out-score on primaries while the Knight player runs out of answers.
302: Built around Huron Blackheart leading Red Corsairs Raiders with Chosen hammers, a Dark Commune psychic support stack, and Accursed Cultists as a disposable screening mass, this is Huron's Marauders — the February 2026 Red Corsairs detachment that folds transport-delivered elite strikers into a body-count scoring engine. The win condition is using Masters of the Maelstrom's mission-tactic flexibility to score secondaries the opponent can't predict while Chosen drop out of transports onto priority targets with Pactbound-style crit stacking, and Accursed Cultist blobs hold every objective the opponent doesn't actively contest. It punishes static gunlines and low-activation vehicle lists brutally — the sheer body count and multi-wave delivery means a Grizzled Company Russ tank or Knight chassis can't clear objectives fast enough to stop the scoring clock. Fast mobile lists with AP-3+ anti-vehicle firepower crack it open, because losing the transport layer mid-table exposes the Chosen to open-field shooting before they reach their targets.
338: Built around swarms of War Dog Stalkers, Karnivores, and Executioners — the Houndpack Lance Wardog spam template — with a Knight Despoiler anchor and Nurglings providing cheap screening. This list wins by flooding the table with 10+ fast T7-8 chassis, using the Stalker's AP-3+ anti-tank output and Karnivore melee to eliminate priority targets on turn 1-2, then scoring primary through sheer activation count while the opponent's fire is split across too many hulls to efficiently clear. Its 4+ invuln stack across every Wardog chassis punishes elite low-volume lists — Mobile Toolbox and Aspect Host-style lists simply can't generate enough high-AP attacks to trade efficiently against 10-12 models with invuln saves, and the activation gap crushes objective scoring races. However, mid-board melee tarpits crack it open: War Horde Boyz mobs and Beast Snagga Squighogs close the distance on turn 1-2, lock Wardogs in combat where they can't shoot, and grind hull points faster than a 5-to-12-activation matchup can recover.
303: Possessed, Obliterators, Chaos Terminators, Chosen, and Legionaries form a dense, crit-stacking Pactbound Zealots core where Dark Pact elevates nearly every activation into a Devastating Wounds threat, delivered forward in Rhinos and Land Raiders. The engine is volume scoring through sustained battleline presence — Possessed drop out of transports and Dark Pact into key targets with Devastating Wounds mortals, while Obliterators and Terminators anchor flanks and Raptors chase secondaries, grinding primary across all five objectives from turn 2 onward. This list punishes low-activation vehicle lists like Infernal Lance and Mont'ka, where the 12-15 activation gap forces opponents into either spreading fire inefficiently or ceding primary ground entirely. It struggles hard against AM Grizzled Company and similar blast-heavy gunlines that pop the transport shell on turn 1, stranding the Possessed hammer squads in the open before they can Dark Pact anything meaningful.
337: Built around Knight Despoilers paired with a Beasts of Nurgle and Nurglings daemon-soup screen — this is the Iconoclast Fiefdom expression of Chaos Knights, not a pure big-knight gunline. The daemon chaff creates an effectively unkillable tarpit wall (Beasts of Nurgle regenerate wounds, Nurglings screen deepstrike) that protects the Knights' flanks while Despoiler Gatling Cannons and War Dog Karnivores deliver the AP-3+ kill package at 24" or less. It wins by using the Nurgle screen to deny melee engagement on its own terms — the Knights dictate when they fight, farm primary behind the tarpit, and spike priority targets with concentrated Melta and Gatling fire once the opponent has burned resources into unkillable Beasts. It punishes slow durable lists like Virulent Vectorium and Aspect Host that can't outrun the knights or out-trade the daemon screen's regeneration, and the 4+ invuln plus daemonic FNP stacking absorbs return fire that would fold a pure-vehicle list. Its weakness is mass-activation infantry hordes — War Horde Orks or AM Recon Element simply flood objectives faster than five activations can contest, and the Nurgle screen, however durable, occupies the Knights in melee while the opponent scores freely on the flanks.
339: Built around Chaos Cerastus Knight Lancers and Knight Rampagers as the melee vanguard, backed by a Knight Tyrant and Despoiler for fire support, this is the Infernal Lance archetype running its full TITANIC roster rather than the Wardog-heavy variant. The engine is speed-plus-layered-defense: 14"+ move Lancers with 4+ invuln from ion shields close to Melta range or charge engagement on turn 1-2, spiking AP-3+ and Lethal Hits triggers into priority targets while the Tyrant's heavy weapons strip hull points from anything that tries to stand at range. It punishes Mid-T Brawler and Mass Volume Horde lists hardest — the Lancer's speed denies the tarpit close, and the Tyrant's Blast weapons delete infantry screens before the mob can lock the chassis in melee. The achilles heel is activation-count pressure from Transport Infantry and mobile deepstrike threats that can swarm objectives the three-to-five activation roster simply cannot contest simultaneously, and concentrated Melta from opposing anti-armour lists can crack the 4+ invuln before the Lancers pay their points back.
300: Built around Chaos Predator Destructors laying down Assault Cannon and Lascannon fire from behind a screen of Noise Marines, Legionaries, and Rhino-mounted infantry, this is a Pactbound Zealots-style transport-mech gunline that blends mid-range vehicle firepower with battleline bodies forward. The plan is to park Predators in a supported second line while Rhino-delivered Legionaries and Chaos Bikers claim objectives turn 1-2, using the Predators' volume fire to punish anything that tries to dig the scoring units out. It punishes slow mid-board infantry lists — War Horde mobs and AM Recon Element blobs can't close the distance before Assault Cannon fire with Sustained Hits 1 starts stripping models, and Chaos Biker harassment locks down secondary scoring lanes. It cracks open against dedicated anti-armour pressure: Melta-range Knights or Mont'ka Crisis Suits delete Predators before they can dictate the board, and without the full Pactbound crit-stack efficiency the list bleeds primaries when its vehicles go down in turns 1-2.
295: Built around Gladiator Lancers and Desolation Squads as the long-range fire base, Deathwing Knights as the armored melee hammer, and Inceptors for mobile pressure, this is the Lion's Blade Task Force playing a hybrid game — planted AP-3+ firepower backed by a durable Terminator anvil. The plan is to use Lancer anti-tank shooting and Desolation indirect fire to strip opposing vehicles and characters at range while Deathwing Knights, buffed by the Ancient in Terminator Armour, threaten the midfield with 2+/4++ resilience that forces the opponent to choose between answering the shooting or the melee threat. Scout screens buy time for the Lancers to dictate the first two turns, and Inceptors clean up objective contests the Terminator brick is too slow to reach. It punishes static gunlines and low-mobility T7-9 chassis lists that can't disengage from both threat vectors simultaneously, but fast skimmer lists and deepstrike-heavy mobile toolbox armies exploit the list's middling movement by denying the Lancer firing arcs and bypassing the Scout screen to isolate the expensive Deathwing Knights before they can contribute.
293: Built around Land Speeder Vengeances and Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes backed by a Deathwing Knights hammer, Lion's Blade Task Force runs a hybrid 1st/2nd Company shell that blends fast-moving fire support with elite melee delivery. It scores by using the Speeders' Assault-keyword plasma and Hurricane Bolter fire to strip screening infantry and mid-range threats while the Deathwing Knights — dropped via Teleport Strike or transported forward — punch through whatever survives into the objective zone. The combination of S8 AP-2 volume fire from the Speeders and 2+/4++ Deathwing Knights with Lethal Hits on their maces means static gunlines and mid-toughness brawlers get traded apart on both axes simultaneously. The list cracks when faced with concentrated AP-3+ anti-armour or fast mobile threats that can match the Speeders' movement and strip the 1st-Company hammer of its screen before it lands — T'au Mont'ka and Chaos Knights Infernal Lance in particular can delete the speeder chassis before it dictates engagement range.
282: Mortarion's Hammer built around Foetid Bloat-Drones with Heavy Blight Launchers, Myphitic Blight-Haulers, and a Poxwalker screen anchored by Deathshroud Terminators and a Lord of Contagion. The engine is a rolling mid-board push: Poxwalkers sticky objectives and absorb attrition while the Bloat-Drones and Blight-Haulers pour Lethal Hits indirect fire into anything that contests, with Deathshroud dropping in via deep strike to punish overextension. T7-8 chassis backed by Disgustingly Resilient and Contagion debuffs makes this list genuinely hard to clear efficiently — it punishes mid-range shooting armies that can't crack T7+ through degraded AP, and Poxwalker blobs shrug off blast templates that would delete lighter screens. Concentrated AP-3+ Melta from Knights or Mont'ka Battlesuits cuts straight through the vehicle stack before Contagion can degrade their accuracy, and fast mobile lists that deny the Blight-Drone firing arc entirely leave the gunline scoring behind on primary.
301: Built around Vashtorr the Arkifane leading a wall of Forgefiends, Venomcrawlers, Helbrutes, and Chaos Vindicators, this is the Soulforged Warpack's daemon-engine-dominant expression — every slot a machine, every machine a Dark Pact trigger. The engine scores by advancing the entire chassis line forward under Vashtorr's buff aura, invoking Dark Pact's +1 to wound on ranged to let Forgefiend Hades Autocannons and Vindicator Demolisher Cannons punch through T7-9 reliably, while Venomcrawlers and Helbrutes absorb counter-charges and generate secondary scoring through sheer board presence. It punishes static gunlines and transport-delivery armies that can't clear T7-9 multi-wound chassis efficiently — a Russ company or Rhino-rush list that commits its anti-tank budget to one big chassis gets run over by five more behind it. The weakness is activation-gap pressure from mass-infantry hordes and fast melee lists: a 30-Boyz mob or a Subterranean Assault deepstrike that locks multiple engines in melee simultaneously starves the shooting engine of its output before Dark Pact can convert wounds into game-deciding damage.
294: Built around Ravenwing Command Squad, Outrider Squads, and Ravenwing Black Knights led by Sammael, this is Company of Hunters at its most committed — a fast-moving mounted Dark Angels force that floods the board with T5 bikes carrying twin bolt rifles, plasma talons, and Corvus hammers across a 14"+ movement profile. It wins by leveraging sheer activation volume and mobility to contest every objective simultaneously while Sammael's aura buffs push Sustained Hits and charge-reroll synergies across the bike-heavy roster. Against planted gunlines and slow mid-board brawlers, the speed advantage is decisive — the list dictates engagement range, farms secondaries with ease, and punishes anything that can't pivot fast enough to address threats from multiple angles at once. The weakness is anti-armour weight: this list carries minimal AP-3+ punch and no meaningful dedicated anti-tank, meaning T8+ vehicle lists and layered-invuln elites absorb the bike shooting without serious concern and grind the scoring race back in their favor.
292: Built around Deathwing Knights, Inner Circle Companions, and Judiciar-led Assault Intercessors with jump packs anchored by Ballistus Dreadnought fire support, this is the Inner Circle Task Force's Unforgiven elite-melee core trying to function as a combined-arms list. The engine is delivering 2+/4++ Deathwing Knights and Companions into melee via the Inner Circle's teleport and deep-strike options while the Ballistus Dreadnought and Intercessors hold objectives and generate chip damage — scoring primary through positional body count and finishing with concentrated elite melee. It punishes mid-range brawler lists and infantry blobs that can't efficiently clear T5-6 models with 4++ saves before the Deathwing charge lands, and the Judiciar's Execution Force ability delays counter-charges long enough for the melee chain to complete. The scattered playstyle axes tell the real story though — this list sits between skirmish fire, gunline, and melee delivery without committing fully to any engine, and a 44% win rate reflects what happens when costly elite hammers that need to teleport safely onto objectives face mobile lists or anti-armour volume that strips the Deathwing before they can swing.
284: Built around Plague Marines delivered in Chaos Rhinos, buffed by a Malignant Plaguecaster and Biologus Putrifier, the Virulent Vectorium plays a Rhino-rush attrition game where every objective your units die on stays yours. The engine is sticky-objective control: disgorge buffed Plague Marines onto mid-board markers, trigger Dark Pact crit-stacking with Putrifier-enhanced Blight Grenades for the damage spike, and let Disgustingly Resilient plus Contagion debuffs bleed the opponent dry trying to dislodge T5 3+ bodies that refuse to give up ground. It punishes static Heavy Gunline lists hard — Russ companies can't clear a Plague Marine squad per turn once Contagion is active, and sticky objectives mean even a half-cleared unit keeps scoring. Mobile anti-armour threats crack it open, however; concentrated AP-3 Melta fire kills the Rhinos before they deliver, leaving Plague Marines walking forward into a firing line that outruns the Contagion aura entirely.
285: Built around a triple Plagueburst Crawler core directed by a Lord of Virulence, with Foetid Bloat-Drones and Myphitic Blight-Haulers as mobile mid-board enforcers and Blightlord Terminators holding the backline behind a Poxwalker screen, this is Mortarion's Hammer at its most vehicle-heavy. The engine scores by using indirect S8 AP-2 Plague Mortar fire to clear screens and force saves through cover turn after turn, while the Bloat-Drones and Blight-Haulers close to mid-board to deny deep-strike lanes and lock down objectives with sticky-objective protection from the Virulent Vectorium detachment rule. It punishes static Heavy Gunline lists and Mass Volume Horde armies brutally — blast templates ignore cover on infantry blobs and the Lord of Virulence's Lethal Hits aura on the Crawlers means even T7-9 vehicles start taking reliable wounds through AP-2 indirect. Against Mobile Anti-Armour opponents packing concentrated AP-3+ Melta, however, the T9 Crawler chassis crumbles faster than the indirect output can compensate, and the list's near-zero movement loading means it cannot reposition to avoid the focus fire.
354: Built around Deathwatch Terminator Squads and Veterans backed by Storm Speeder Thunderstrikes and Indomitor Kill Teams, this is the Black Spear Task Force running a hard-hitting mech-infantry hybrid that floods the board with kill teams and elite bodies delivered via Rhino. The engine is objective attrition through activation density — Infiltrators claim forward ground turn 1 while Terminators and Veterans push out of transports to contest mid-table, with Thunderstrikes providing S9 AP-2 anti-armour reach that forces the opponent to split resources. It punishes slower positional lists by out-activating them on objectives, converting the Deathwatch special-issue ammunition variety and Mission Tactics flexibility into per-turn scoring leads that compound across the game. It cracks under concentrated high-AP shooting that strips transports before the cargo can deploy, and elite-melee lists that win the subsequent fight once Terminators are walking rather than riding.
305: Built around Ravagers, an Archon-led Incubi hammer, Kabalite Warriors in Venoms, and Scourges with heavy weapons, this is a pure Kabal-flavored Drukhari list running the Kabalite Cartel detachment — the mono-Kabal expression of Realspace Raiders without the Harlequin or Wych Cult splash. The plan is to advance Venoms into mid-range firing positions turn one, stripping infantry screens with Splinter Cannon volume while Ravager Dark Lances target key vehicles or characters, then deliver Incubi out of transports to finish whatever the shooting softened. It punishes planted gunlines and low-mobility armies that can't deny Venom firing arcs or escape the Archon's Lethal Hits-stacking aura, converting the fire-and-fade tempo advantage into a scoring lead on secondaries. The 42% win rate exposes the core weakness: any list that matches or exceeds Venom movement speed — Knights, Mont'ka Crisis suits, or deepstriking melee — cracks the fragile T5 transport chassis at range before the Incubi ever disembark, collapsing the delivery engine entirely.
283: Built around Nurglings, Plaguebearers, Beasts of Nurgle, and Rotigus as summoned-daemon anchors alongside a Great Unclean One and Foetid Bloat-Drone heavy blight launcher fire support, this is Virulent Vectorium running a daemonic summoning engine rather than the conventional Plague Marine brick. The plan is flooding mid-board objectives with disposable Nurgling and Plaguebearer bodies — sticky-objective rules mean each daemon unit locks scoring even as it dies — while Rotigus and the GUO project threat forward and Bloat-Drones chip opponents out of engagement range with Lethal Hits indirect pressure. The layered defensive stack of Disgustingly Resilient-equivalent FNP on daemon units, combined with raw model volume, punishes armies that commit expensive activations to clear chaff — mid-T brawler hordes and transport-infantry lists waste precious shooting trimming bodies that respawn or score anyway. The build cracks open against concentrated AP-3+ Mobile Anti-Armour fire and anything with blast templates: Knights with Avenger Gatling Cannons and Demolisher Siege Cannons delete multiple Plaguebearer/Nurgling models per activation, and the summoning engine can't generate bodies faster than a focused Russ tank company removes them.
307: Built around multiple Talos Pain Engines supported by Wracks, a Haemonculus, and Raider delivery, this is a Coven-flavored Drukhari list that swaps the faction's typical glass-cannon skimmer identity for T7 monstrous creatures with 4+ invulnerable saves and Feel No Pain stacking via Haemonculus buffs. The engine is grinding mid-board objectives with durable Talos bricks while Scourges and Mandrakes handle secondary scoring and chip damage, leaning on the Coven's defensive layering to absorb return fire rather than kiting away from it. The layered T7/4++/FNP profile punishes lists that rely on volume S4-5 fire to clear objectives, particularly Mass Volume Horde blobs and Mid-T Brawler mobs that can't efficiently wound through the Talos statline. The 42% win rate exposes the core problem: this build asks Drukhari to stand still and trade, but it lacks the AP-3+ concentration to threaten Knights or heavy vehicles, and fast Mobile Anti-Armour lists crack the Talos chassis with Melta before the Haemonculus FNP engine can compensate.
304:
Spectacle of Spite is built around Succubi-led Wych Cult units — Wyches in Raiders and Venoms, Hellions and Reavers ranging wide — delivering a Raider-mech shell that reads like Realspace Raiders but keyed entirely around Combat Drug cycling and Pain Token accumulation.

The engine is tempo-and-volume: advance Venoms and Raiders into mid-board turn 1, chip Pain Tokens off expendable Hellions and Reavers, then spike a Wych unit with an active Combat Drug to punch well above its points value in melee while the skimmer chassis holds objectives by sheer OC weight.

It punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox lists hard — Russ tanks can't fire into a list that repositions 14-16" every turn, and Wych melee locks anything that can't fall back cleanly — while Pistol-armed Wyches and Reavers keep generating chip damage to fuel the Pain Token loop.

Concentrated AP-3+ anti-armour from Knight chassis or Mont'ka Battlesuits cracks open the Raider delivery system before the Combat Drug rotation can pay off, and without a reliable invulnerable save on any transport, one well-sequenced anti-vehicle volley can strand three Wych units in the open.
306: Built around the Solitaire, Reavers, Scourges, Hellions, and Incubi delivered in Venoms, Reaper's Wager folds the best Harlequin units into a Drukhari skimmer shell — fast, fragile platforms stacked with Pistol and Assault-keyword firepower that never stand still long enough to be punished. The engine is tempo and kite: Venoms advance and fire Splinter Cannons while Scourges with heavy weapons spike priority targets, Reavers slash across objectives for secondary scoring, and the Solitaire drops into isolated characters to remove them with Precision before the opponent can react. It punishes planted gunlines and slow durable-grind lists that can't dictate engagement range, using 14–16" move platforms to deny Russ firing arcs and bleed Death Guard off objectives without ever accepting a fair trade. It cracks open against anything that matches its movement and brings AP-3+ anti-vehicle fire — Knights or Mont'ka Crisis Suits can pace the skimmers and pop Venoms before the contents escape, collapsing the delivery engine entirely.
327: Built around a Winged Daemon Prince of Slaanesh, Noise Marines in Chaos Rhinos, and Infractors backed by Lord Exultant and Lord Kakophonist buffs, this is the Court of the Phoenician delivering Slaanesh-marked firepower and mobile melee on a transport-mech chassis. The plan is to push Rhinos into midfield by turn two, disgorge Noise Marines and Infractors onto contested objectives, and spike damage through Lord Kakophonist's Cacophony aura and Sonic Blaster volume — scoring primary through sustained body presence while the Winged Daemon Prince hunts isolated characters or flanks into backfield objectives. It punishes slow, static gunlines and low-model-count anti-armour lists that can't clear multiple disembarked squads per turn and lack the activation density to contest every marker. However, with a below-50% win rate it struggles against anything that pops the Rhinos early — Russ Demolisher volleys or concentrated AP-3+ anti-vehicle fire strands the contents on foot and collapses the scoring engine before it fires.
329: Built around triple Defilers, a winged Daemon Prince of Slaanesh, and Rhino-delivered Infractors and Tormentors stacked under a Lord Exultant, this is the Emperor's Children Carnival of Excess pushing a daemon-engine-forward beatdown variant of the transport-rush shell. The plan is to use the Defilers' S14 AP-3 Battle Cannons to crack transports and elite infantry at range while the Rhinos disgorge Infractors into mid-board, letting the winged Daemon Prince and Lord Exultant synergies chain Dark Pact crit-triggers across both the shooting and melee phases. It punishes static gunlines and mid-T brawlers hardest — the Defiler's Blast output clears infantry blobs while the Prince's 14" move and 4+ invuln let it spike a key target before the opponent can concentrate fire. Lists with concentrated AP-3+ Melta at range — Mont'ka Battlesuits, Chaos Knights Infernal Lance — can strip Defilers off the board before the Dark Pact engine comes online, and the relatively shallow wound pool across three T9 chassis means focus fire collapses the damage output fast.
291: Built around Gargoyles, Hyperadapted Raveners, Lictors, and Deathleaper, Final Day leans into its unique Tyranid-allied datasheet access to field a swarming mid-board threat that no pure GSC detachment can replicate. The engine is volume-on-objectives: Gargoyle mobs claim and contest primary while Raveners and Lictors deepstrike or infiltrate into the opponent's scoring pieces, and Achilles Ridgerunners provide the anti-vehicle weight to suppress any armoured counter. It punishes static gunlines and low-activation-count vehicle lists that can't clear T4-5 wound pools spread across 8-12 distinct units simultaneously, especially when Ridgerunner indirect fire denies safe positioning. However, it struggles against Heavy Gunline Toolbox and Layered Lethal Combat opponents — Blast templates and Lethal Hits weapon volume systematically strip Gargoyle and Ravener bodies faster than the swarm can contest objectives in return.
328: Built around Flawless Blades as the hammer unit, Lucius the Eternal as their mandatory character attachment, and a supporting cast of Infractors, Tormentors, and Noise Marines delivered in Rhinos and Land Raiders, this is the Emperor's Children Carnival of Excess in its most transport-committed expression. The engine is Lucius-led Flawless Blades crashing out of a Land Raider into the opponent's most expensive unit — stacking the Slaanesh crit-fishing and Excess of Violence triggers to delete a key piece per turn while Noise Marines and Tormentors hold midfield objectives through sheer sonic-weapon volume. It punishes slower static lists and anything running clustered elite infantry: the Flawless Blades' AP-2 melee combined with Lucius's fight-twice mechanic overloads 3+ armor saves that can't spread out behind a screen, and the transport shell makes the delivery nearly impossible to pre-empt with shooting. The list's 42% win rate reflects its core fragility — pop the Land Raider before the Blades disembark and the entire turn-2 spike evaporates, leaving Noise Marines and Tormentors to grind a game they weren't built to win alone.
290: Built around Atalan Jackals, Achilles Ridgerunners, Goliath Rockgrinders, and Neophyte Hybrid blobs screened by Acolyte Hybrids with hand flamers, this is the Outlander Claw's vehicle-and-cult-mob hybrid — a mechanised cult column that floods the board with both bodies and fast chassis simultaneously. The engine runs on raw OC saturation: Neophyte blobs claim and hold objectives while Jackals and Rockgrinders race forward to contest secondaries and threaten flanks, with the Benefictus providing character-support precision to keep key units functional under pressure. It punishes slow static lists — Heavy Gunline Toolbox and planted infantry hordes — that can't reposition fast enough to strip objectives from both the vehicle wave and the footslogging screen arriving behind it, forcing inefficient trade decisions every turn. It struggles against concentrated AP-3+ anti-armour and Lethal Hits firepower that can simultaneously strip the thin-skinned vehicle chassis and blast through the T3 Neophyte screens before the body-count advantage compounds into a scoring lead.
353:
Built around Fortis Kill Teams, Indomitor Kill Teams, and Incursor Squads cycling through Special Issue Ammunition, Black Spear Task Force is a multi-threat Marine mech list that exploits the SIA selector to respec its damage profile every shooting phase — Kraken Bolts for AP-2 reach, Hellfire for anti-horde, Vengeance for anti-vehicle — across a dense roster of mixed-profile infantry bricks.

The engine is sustained primary scoring backed by precision threat removal: Fortis and Indomitor Kill Teams disembark from Impulsor and Rhino delivery to claim and hold mid-board objectives while SIA-spammed Intercessor and Incursor units suppress whatever the opponent commits to contest them, with the Judiciar locking priority targets in a fight they can't win.

The multi-axis SIA toolkit punishes static single-profile armies hardest — Heavy Gunline Toolbox lists and mass infantry hordes find that every profile they rely on has a bolt round specifically designed to gut it, and the high activation count from mixed kill-team compositions keeps primary-scoring pressure constant.

Fast armies with layered invulnerable saves and kite-friendly movement crack it open — Drukhari Raider chassis and Aspect Host stay outside optimal SIA range, forcing Deathwatch into unfavorable advance-fire compromises, and the lack of a meaningful long-range anti-vehicle answer means anything with a 4+ invuln and 14"+ movement can dictate engagement range all game.
289: Built around Aberrants led by an Abominant, Purestrain Genestealers, and Biophagus-buffed melee blocks delivered into position with Achilles Ridgerunner fire support, this is the Biosanctic Broodsurge in its purest expression — a T5 melee-hammer list that weaponizes the Aberrant's volume of Rending attacks and the Abominant's buff aura to delete elite infantry and mid-weight vehicles on contact. The engine is straightforward: Patriarch-buffed Purestrains and Aberrant bricks claim and hold midfield objectives through raw wound pool and 5+ invuln durability, while Ridgerunners chip vehicles at range and Biophagus keeps the melee blocks healthy turn over turn. It punishes static mid-T lists and low-activation vehicle gunlines hardest — Aberrants at T5 with a 5+ invuln absorb blast templates well enough to close, then the Rending-volume swing clears whatever contested the objective. Its genuine weakness is layered-defense grind lists and fast skimmer kite: Death Guard Vectorium's Disgustingly Resilient and Contagion debuffs blunt the Aberrant charge math badly, and Drukhari Reaper's Wager can fire-and-fade out of charge range indefinitely.
330: Built around Fulgrim leading a swarm of Chaos Spawn, Maulerfiends, and Infractors with Noise Marine fire support, this is the Court of the Phoenician expression of Emperor's Children — a fast, diverse melee roster delivered via momentum rather than transport shell. The engine runs Fulgrim and the Lord Exultant stacking Slaanesh-mark synergies onto Infractors and Spawn blobs, flooding mid-board objectives turn 1 with high-model-count units while Maulerfiends pin anything that tries to push back, scoring primary through sheer activation volume and OC saturation. It punishes static gunlines and transport-infantry mirrors that can't handle simultaneous threats from multiple T5-7 melee vectors at once — a Russ company or Pactbound Possessed stack struggles to address Spawn chaff, a Maulerfiend, and Infractors charging from three angles in the same turn. The list cracks open when fast anti-armour concentrates on the Maulerfiends early and dedicated Lethal Hits shooting — Plague Belchers, Dark Reaper volleys with Preternatural Precision, Avenger Gatling Cannons — chews through the low-save Spawn and Infractor bodies faster than Fulgrim's aura can compensate.
343: Built around Nemesis Dreadknights led by a Grand Master NDK, Purifiers, Interceptors, and a Brotherhood Librarian, this is Warpbane Task Force running a fast-moving elite melee-gunline hybrid that leans hard on the NDK chassis as its primary damage delivery system. The engine is getting 2-3 NDKs into mid-board by turn 2 via their 12" movement and teleport-strike options, using the Grand Master's re-roll aura to maximize AP-3+ Doomfist and Shunt attacks while Purifiers and Strike Squads contest objectives in their wake. It punishes slow durable-grind lists and planted gunlines — Heavy Gunline and Transport Infantry specifically — because NDKs match or outpace most non-skimmer platforms in speed while hitting hard enough to crack T7-9 chassis, and the layered 5+ invuln plus psychic defenses absorb the return fire. Against faster skimmer kite lists and mobile toolbox melee, however, the low model count and limited objective-coverage infantry mean it bleeds primary points steadily while chasing units it can't catch or getting tarpitted before the NDK punch lands cleanly.
317: Built around Subductor Squads and Imperial Navy Breachers as the battleline engine, Watch Master-led Deathwatch Kill Teams as the elite hammer, and Sanctifiers providing layered defensive support inside Imperial Rhinos, this is Imperialis Fleet running a dense multi-faction mech-infantry package. The plan is to deliver Breachers and Subductors onto objectives via Rhino rush while the Kill Teams spike off isolated characters via Precision crits, grinding primary through sheer activation volume across a wide datasheet roster. The multi-faction toolbox punishes lower-model-count lists — Knights, skimmer kite armies, and heavy-gunline builds all struggle to contest enough objectives against a list that floods the midfield with durable, Rhino-protected bodies backed by 4+ invuln support characters. However, the 39% win rate tells the real story: this jack-of-all-trades package lacks the damage ceiling to clear entrenched durable-scoring lists, and anything with blast templates or massed AP-2 fire strips the fragile Rhino shells before the cargo can engage.
342: Built around Paladin Squads and Brotherhood Terminators led by Brother-Captain and Grand Master Voldus, this is the Hallowed Conclave's signature Terminator-brick expression — bulky 2+/4++ elite infantry that teleport into midfield and refuse to move. The plan is to deep strike Terminators and Paladins onto contested objectives, leverage Voldus's psychic buffing and the Brotherhood Librarian's support strats to spike damage through Lethal Hits and Sustained Hits 1 on key activations, then outscore opponents by holding ground their shooting can't efficiently clear. The 2+/4++ defensive profile punishes low-AP volume lists — skimmer-fire kite armies and horde gunlines bounce off Terminator armor, and the Strike Squad screen denies easy deepstrike counters against the brick. However, the concentrated elite model count and reliance on Voldus and the Librarian for buff chains means focused AP-3+ anti-tank overload — Mont'ka Melta, Infernal Lance Gatling Cannons, or Soulforged Dark Pact Devastation — cracks the invuln stack and collapses the scoring engine faster than the small activation count can recover.
279: Built around Einhyr Hearthguard bricks led by Kâhl and Einhyr Champion characters, screened by Hernkyn Pioneers and backed by Brôkhyr Thunderkyn fire support, this is the Hearthband index detachment doing exactly what Votann were designed to do. The engine is Judgement Token accumulation: stack Tokens on priority targets via Kâhl and Pioneer spotting, then delete them with Hearthguard hammers and Thunderkyn mass S6 AP-2 fire hitting on 2s with Lethal Hits triggers from Judged status. It punishes mid-range brawler lists and static gunlines through the combination of T5 3+ armor on Hearthguard, high-volume Lethal Hits output that ignores FNP math, and Pioneers' speed providing secondary-scoring reach that slow attrition lists can't match. Fast melee delivery and mobile anti-armour lists crack it open, since committing the Hearthguard brick forward exposes the expensive character stack to alpha-strike focus fire, and without Tokens pre-loaded the Votann damage engine stalls when the Kâhl dies before the trade connects.
281: Built around Sagitaurs, Hearthkyn Warriors, and a Hekaton Land Fortress anchoring the line, this is a Hearthband-flavored mechanised combined-arms list that leans harder into mobile firepower than the Mercenary Oathband's elite-unit focus. The engine is mid-board volume pressure: Sagitaurs fire on the advance via Assault-keyword weapons while Ironkin Steeljacks with Heavy Volkanite Disintegrators and the Hekaton deliver sustained AP-2 fire, with Brôkhyr Iron-Masters keeping key chassis operational long enough to grind primary on attrition. Its T5-6 chassis, decent wound pools, and respectable shooting volume punish Mid-T Brawler lists that can't absorb sustained Volkanite damage and lack the anti-vehicle tools to pop Sagitaurs before they close. Fast skimmer lists and genuine mobile anti-armour threats crack it open, however — Drukhari Raiders outrange the Volkanite sweet spot, and concentrated AP-3+ Melta from Knights or Mont'ka Crisis Suits burns through the Hekaton before the Iron-Master can patch the hull points back.
280: Built around Cthonian Beserks as the melee hammer, Earthshakers for fire support, and a Hekaton Land Fortress as the armoured delivery chassis, this is a Hearthband-style mixed-arms list that leans hard into the Votann's T5 brawler identity. The plan is to advance Beserks into mid-board under cover of Earthshaker bombardment and Memnyr Strategist's Judgement tokens, forcing opponents to either weather the charge or over-commit to clearing the screen while the Hekaton threatens a flank. It punishes low-activation vehicle lists — Knights and Mont'ka Tau especially — because the Beserks' volume of T5 attacks with Judgement-stacked hit bonuses can crack T9-11 chassis when the Hekaton delivers them into range. It struggles badly against fast skimmer kite lists and blast-heavy gunlines, where the Beserks' moderate movement (no native deepstrike or transport guarantee) leaves them stranded mid-table eating Russ Demolisher templates before they ever swing.
278: Built around a Hekaton Land Fortress ferrying Ironkin Steeljacks into melee, backed by Brôkhyr Thunderkyn heavy weapon teams and a Kapricus Carrier delivering Hernkyn Yaegirs for secondary harassment, this is Leagues of Votann's Mercenary Oathband at its most aggressive. The engine is transport delivery: the Hekaton plants on a midfield objective while the Steeljacks disembark and engage T5-7 targets with melee volume, the Memnyr Strategist cycling Oaths of Vengeance to stack Crit triggers on the kill chain, while Thunderkyn blast anything that tries to shoot the transport out from under the plan. It punishes static gunlines and mid-range vehicle spam brutally — the Hekaton's T13 chassis absorbs focused fire that would clear a lighter transport, buying the Steeljacks a full activation to deliver AP-2 melee volume directly into firing positions. Lists with fast melee-threat delivery that can race the Hekaton to the mid-board — particularly War Horde mob flooding or Subterranean Assault deepstrikes — can clog the landing zone before the Steeljacks unload, converting the list's forward momentum into a traffic jam it can't shoot its way out of.
341: Built around Razorbacks delivering Purifiers and Strike Squads under the Grand Master in Nemesis Dreadknight's aura, this is a transport-mech Grey Knights list that plays closer to Rhino-rush than the Dreadknight-castle the name implies — Castellan Crowe leading Purifiers out of the back hatch is the signature activation. The engine is fire-on-the-move Razorback fire (Assault-keyword heavy bolters and lascannons advancing into range) combined with Interceptor Squad teleport threats contesting midfield, all scoring primary through multi-objective presence while the GMNDK anchors the center as a 4++ melee deterrent. This profile punishes static Heavy Gunline Toolbox lists badly — Razorbacks match or exceed Russ firing arcs in mobility, and the GMNDK's 4++ plus Storm Bolter volume make it cheap to contest objectives the opponent can't reach and expensive to clear. The weak matchup is massed Lethal Hits from Layered Lethal Combat lists — Plague Marine Contagion debuffs strip the Grey Knights' already-modest armor saves while Disgustingly Resilient means the reciprocal trade doesn't clear Plague Marine squads cleanly, and the Razorback chassis (T7, 3+ no invuln) melts under focused AP-3+ attention.
314: Built around Necron Warriors in Ghost Arks with Orikan the Diviner, Royal Warden, and Illuminor Szeras stacking reanimation and stat buffs, this is a Reanimation Protocol durability engine dressed up as an objective-holding toolbox. It wins by planting large Warrior blobs — buffed to S5-6 via Szeras and protected by Orikan's temporal anomaly rolls — on primary objectives while Canoptek Tomb Crawlers provide melee screening and mobile anti-armour support, grinding the scoring clock through raw wound attrition rather than damage spikes. The layered durability punishes shooting-heavy lists that can't produce enough volume to overcome reanimating T4 models with 4+ armor and FNP-equivalent recursion, making Russ tank companies and static Marine gunlines especially inefficient — they kill the same Warrior twice without clearing the objective. Aggressive melee armies and Transport Infantry rushes crack it open by overwhelming the screen before reanimation resolves and contesting objectives with bodies the Warrior blob can't evict fast enough.
312: Built around Doomsday Arks as long-range anti-armour anchors, the Silent King as a near-unkillable command presence, and Canoptek Wraiths delivering melee pressure, this is Starshatter Arsenal at its current tournament peak. The engine runs Doomsday Arks (S14 AP-4 D6+2 shots at full charge) backed by Technomancer reanimation support, using Wraiths and Flayed One harassment to deny opponent repositioning while the Arks delete vehicles and elite infantry from range. It punishes static Heavy Gunline and skimmer-fire lists that can't answer both the 24"+ Doomsday Cannon arcs and the 4+ invuln Wraith threat closing simultaneously — two vectors that Russ tanks and Raider chassis each solve poorly in isolation. Its primary crack point is concentrated Melta or AP-3+ mobile anti-armour: Knights and Mont'ka Crisis Battlesuits can close range fast enough to threaten the Ark chassis before Technomancer reanimation keeps pace, collapsing the shooting engine that the entire scoring plan depends on.
350: Built around wall-to-wall Armiger Warglaives and Helverins backed by Knight Warden and Knight Defender support chassis, this is a Skyreaper Lance-adjacent activation-count swarm that floods the board with T9 light Knights rather than committing to one or two TITANIC anchors. The plan is to overwhelm primary scoring through sheer activation volume — seven-plus Armigers each contesting an objective while Helverin autocannons (S7 AP-2, Sustained Hits 1) strip light infantry and Warglaive Thermal Spears crack anything T8 and below at 12" range, with a Callidus Assassin disrupting key opponent stratagems to protect the swarm's turn-2 commit. It punishes Transport Infantry and Mass Volume Horde lists that can't efficiently trade into seven separate T9 bodies across the board, where activation parity collapses and the opponent runs out of cost-effective removal before objectives tip. The weak spot is anything that out-ranges the 12" Melta envelope — Mont'ka Crisis Battlesuits and Infernal Lance Despoilers with Gatling Cannons can cherry-pick isolated Armigers from 24"+ before the swarm closes distance, and the 5+ invuln means concentrated AP-3 fire deletes a Warglaive per turn without much drama.
352: Built around Knight Castellan, Knight Errant, and Cerastus Knight Lancer chassis — this is a Questoris Companions list running three to five Titanic and heavy Knights with ion shield 4+ invulns across every model and massed AP-3+ firepower from Avenger Gatling Cannons, Thunderstrike Gauntlets, and the Castellan's twin Siegebreaker Cannons. The engine is concentrated target priority at speed: 12"-base movement lets the list dictate range every turn, spiking AP-3 Melta and Gatling volume into the opponent's most dangerous unit before repositioning behind terrain, while the ion shield 4+ invuln and T11-12 chassis absorb the return fire and grind primary scoring through raw OC dominance with three to five activations sitting on objectives. It punishes slow durable lists — Death Guard Vectorium and massed infantry blobs lack the mobility to deny the firing arcs and lack the AP-3+ Melta density to crack multiple T11-12 chassis before falling behind on primary. It cracks open against high-activation mob lists and Transport Infantry, where War Horde Boyz or Pactbound Cultist screens simply have twelve to fifteen activations forcing the Knight player off objectives the moment their five activation slots are committed to shooting rather than contesting.
351: Built around Knight Crusaders, Cerastus Atrapos, and Cerastus Lancers backed by Canis Rex, this is a Questoris Companions-style big-knight gunline running three or four TITANIC chassis with complementary weapon loadouts — Avenger Gatling Cannons and Thermal Cannons on the Crusaders, the Atrapos's Lascutter and Graviton Singularity Cannon for heavy anti-armour, and the Lancer's Shock Lance for melee threat — with a Callidus Assassin tucked in to punish character-dependent lists. The win condition is turn-1 fire-priority dominance: concentrate AP-3+ Melta and Lethal Hits weapon volume onto the opponent's primary anti-tank or character, remove it before the list can function, then outscore on primary while the remaining Knights are too durable to clear efficiently. At 55%+ win rate this punishes mid-table durability lists — T7-9 Death Guard vehicles and CSM Possessed hammers in particular crack under concentrated Thermal Cannon and Graviton fire that bypasses FNP stacks and 5+ invulns through sheer AP and Damage output. The glass ceiling is mob tarpits and activation-gap lists: War Horde Ork blobs close distance and lock the Knights in melee, and Transport Infantry CSM with 12-15 activations simply out-scores three big chassis on primary objectives regardless of how favorable the trades look per unit.
315: Built around a court of C'tan Shards — Transcendent C'tan, the Deceiver, the Void Dragon, and the Nightbringer — Awakened Dynasty fields two to four of the most punishing Monsters in the game, screened by Flayed Ones and a Hexmark Destroyer, exploiting the detachment's permissive list-building to stack godlike profiles that no single army list is designed to answer. The engine is threat saturation: each C'tan forces a different defensive answer — the Void Dragon obliterates vehicles with AP-3+ melee and Enslaved Star Engines, the Nightbringer farms infantry with mortal-wound auras, and the Deceiver repositions your entire threat package mid-game with Grand Illusion — so the opponent either splits focus and loses every trade or concentrates and concedes primary scoring to Flayed Ones and the Hexmark.
