It crushes mid-range shooting lists and anything relying on a single damage type, because no one suite of anti-tank, anti-elite, or anti-infantry tools efficiently answers three different T10–11, 4+ invuln Monsters simultaneously. Layered Lethal Combat walls it out — Death Guard Vectorium's Disgustingly Resilient FNP stack and Plagueburst Crawler indirect fire, or Custodes' 2+/4++ across the board, can absorb C'tan punishment long enough to grind primary while the Plague Marines' sticky objectives deny the scoring the C'tan castle needs to close games.
316: Built around Immortals as the scoring core, Canoptek Doomstalkers as mid-range firepower platforms, and Canoptek Wraiths with Scarab Swarm screens backed by Plasmancer and Technomancer buffs, this is the Canoptek Court detachment doing what its name promises: a Reanimation-fuelled attrition engine with genuine teeth at every range band. The gameplan is to plant Immortal blobs on objectives with Reanimation stacking from Technomancer and Plasmancer support, use Doomstalkers' indirect-capable S10 AP-3 shots to threaten mid-table without exposing the scoring core, and let Wraiths' 4+ invuln act as a mobile denial piece that forces opponents to commit resources to clear. It punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox and Mass Volume Horde lists through activation-count advantage plus the Reanimation loop making each Immortal squad functionally larger than it appears on paper — static gunlines can't generate enough focus fire to clear a unit before it partially refills. Where it struggles is against Mobile Anti-Armour and concentrated AP-3+ Melta pressure: Doomstalkers are T7 with no invuln, and once Knights or Mont'ka Battlesuits start peeling the fire platforms turn one, the scoring core loses its teeth and the win rate reflects it.
313: Built around Skorpekh Destroyers and a Skorpekh Lord leading the melee hammer, Lokhust Heavy Destroyers providing the ranged anti-armour punch, and Ophydian Destroyers as a deepstriking flanking threat, this is the Cursed Legion in full expression — a Destroyer Cult roster where every unit benefits from the +2 Strength chain-buff trigger when any Destroyer Cult unit destroys or halves an enemy. The win condition is a sequenced kill chain: Lokhust Heavies crack a vehicle or elite unit at range to trip the +2 S buff, then Skorpekhs and Ophydians close into the now-exposed backfield targets with T5 bodies and 4+ invulnerable saves locking mid-board objectives while Lychguard hold home. It punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox and static shooting armies hardest — the combination of deepstriking Ophydians threatening flanks plus Skorpekh threat-projection forces a gunline to split fire it can't afford, and Russ tanks can't fall back out of Skorpekh engagement. Mass infantry hordes and Transport Infantry with cultist screens are its ceiling problem — the Destroyer Cult payload is a relatively low model-count melee threat that a sufficiently dense screen absorbs before the +2 S trigger fires on anything meaningful.
359: Built around Flash Gitz and Breaka Boyz delivered by Trukks, backed by Warboss and Beastboss character stacks leading Beast Snagga Boyz, this is War Horde at its most mechanically layered — a Trukk-rush variant that combines the detachment's always-on Sustained Hits 1 across every melee weapon with a Beast Snagga anti-vehicle threat alongside a genuine long-range shooting unit in the Flash Gitz. The engine is activation flooding: Trukks push Breaka Boyz and Beast Snagga Boyz onto midfield objectives turns 1-2 while Flash Gitz chip key targets at range, forcing the opponent to address multiple threat vectors simultaneously while the list outscores on primary through sheer OC volume. It punishes low-model-count anti-armour lists hardest — Knights and Mont'ka-style vehicle builds get swarmed by mobs that contest every objective and lock expensive chassis in melee where Sustained Hits 1 on Breaka Boyz attacks converts reliably into hull damage. Its critical vulnerability is fast kiting fire: Drukhari Raiders and Aeldari Wave Serpents can sit outside charge range, delete the Trukks before disembarkation, and leave the infantry stranded mid-table without ever offering a fair trade.
362: Built around Squighog Boyz, Kill Rig, Beastboss on Squigosaur, and Mozrog Skragbad, this is Da Big Hunt's premier Beast Snagga expression — a T5-7 cavalry-and-monster list that floods the board with high-toughness melee bodies and dedicated anti-vehicle pressure. The engine is volume charging: Squighogs and Beast Snagga Boyz close the gap turn 1 via forward deployment and advance moves, locking opposing vehicles in melee while the Kill Rig dishes out mortal wounds and Beastboss characters stack wound-reroll auras to feed the sustained damage cycle. It punishes low-model-count anti-armour lists like Infernal Lance and Questoris Companions brutally — the sheer activation count buries Knights in tarpits before their Melta range threats can concentrate fire on a single target. Fast-kiting lists crack it open: Drukhari Reaper's Wager and Aeldari Aspect Host simply sit at 24"+ and chip Squighogs with AP-2 fire all game, because without melee contact this list has no damage engine.
336: Built around Terminator Assault Squads and Terminator Squads as the melee hammer, Gladiator Lancers as the long-range anti-armour spine, and Bladeguard Veterans plus a Judiciar as the midfield anvil, this is a 1st Company Task Force or Anvil Siege Force expression that pairs slow elite infantry with planted heavy firepower. The plan is to post Heavy Intercessors and Bladeguard on primary objectives turn 1 while Lancers delete opposing vehicles at range, then walk the Terminators into whatever survives and clean up in melee. It punishes low-model-count anti-armour and skimmer lists that can't efficiently clear T5 2+/4++ bodies in volume, forcing opponents to over-invest fire into durable infantry while the Lancers operate freely. The critical weakness is speed — this list cannot close on fast objective-scoring armies or kiting skimmer builds, and with a sub-35% win rate the activation gap against Transport Infantry and Mass Volume Horde lists bleeds primary scoring turn over turn before the Terminator hammer ever connects.
361: War Horde built around massed Boyz blobs buffered by Painboys, Meganobz hammers, dual Warboss command stacks, and Stormboyz as the fast flanking element — this is Ghazghkull's Warband running the Sustained Hits 1 detachment rule across every unit on the table. The engine is raw OC dominance: 30-Boyz mobs with Painboy Feel No Pain support plant on objectives and refuse to die while Meganobz and the Warboss in Mega Armour deliver a concentrated T5 2+ save hammer into whatever the opponent commits to clearing the screen. It punishes low-activation anti-tank lists and planted gunlines hardest — a 5-vehicle Knight list or an AM Russ company simply can't generate enough blast-template volume to clear multiple 30-Boyz mobs per turn before losing primary on time. The list cracks open against fast fire-and-fade skimmer lists that sit at 24"+ and chip models off the blob without ever entering charge range, and against Lethal Hits shooting (Dark Reapers, Plague weapons, Russ Punishers) that bypasses T5 math and clears mobs faster than the Painboy's 5+ FNP can compensate.
331: Built around Marneus Calgar leading Victrix Honour Guard and Wardens of Ultramar in an Ultramarines midfield anchor, with Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreadnoughts providing the heavy firepower and Uriel Ventris delivering character-hunting Precision kills. This is a Gladius Task Force or Anvil Siege Force shell that scores through sustained primary dominance — Calgar's aura locks the midfield while twin Repulsor Executioners and Ballistus Dreadnoughts delete vehicles and elite infantry at range with AP-3+ macro-cannon and twin lascannon volleys, freeing Victrix and Wardens to hold objectives and body-block. It punishes static heavy gunlines and transport infantry hard, matching their firepower footprint while the Honour Guard's T5 2+/4++ profile absorbs the return fire that would strip a lesser midfield anchor. It cracks open against Mobile Toolbox deepstrike threats and skimmer kite lists — Calgar's bubble is a large target for early Skorpekh or Aberrant teleport plays that collapse the firing line before the Executioners can clear the screen, and the lack of chassis mobility means it cannot chase a fire-and-fade Wave Serpent list that denies optimal firing arcs from deployment.
360: Built around the Big Mek with Shokk Attack Gun as the long-range anchor, supported by Tankbustas, Lootas, Mek support characters, Killa Kans, and Gretchin bodies holding objectives, this is a War Horde-adjacent shooting-heavy Ork list that tries to win through volume fire rather than the usual Sustained Hits 1 melee grind. The plan is to plant Gretchin blobs on objectives for raw OC while the Shokk Attack Gun and Lootas suppress mid-board threats at range and Tankbustas concentrate melta-equivalent anti-tank attention on the opponent's key chassis, scoring primary through sheer body-count advantage rather than fight-phase trading. Against Heavy Gunline Toolbox and Transport Infantry lists it can compete on objective coverage — Gretchin blobs are cheap OC that Russ tanks waste shots clearing, and Tankbustas threaten Rhinos and Land Raiders from behind the Gretchin screen. It falls apart against anything fast and mobile: a 39% win rate signals that Skimmer Skirmish Fire and Mobile Toolbox lists simply kite the planted Shokk Attack Gun out of relevance, and without the melee threat of War Horde's Sustained Hits 1 mobs, there's no mechanism to close the distance and punish that kiting.
335: Built around multiple Vindicators backed by Roboute Guilliman, Marneus Calgar in the Armour of Antilochus, and Victrix Honour Guard, this is an Ironstorm Spearhead-adjacent castle that uses premier Ultramarines characters to anchor a Demolisher Cannon gunline. The core engine is Guilliman's reroll aura stacking with Calgar's command presence to push Vindicator Demolisher Cannons — S14 AP-3 Damage 6, D6+3 Blast — into reliable multi-wound-clear territory each turn while Scout Squads and a Lieutenant screen the deployment and contest secondaries. It punishes static infantry blobs and Transport Infantry lists hard, where Blast templates ignore cover and delete the scoring bodies that Rhino-rush depends on before they can contest primaries. It cracks open against fast mobile threats — Skimmer Skirmish kiting and Mobile Toolbox deepstrike plays can isolate Vindicators in melee or stay outside the 24" Demolisher arc entirely, stranding Guilliman's reroll bubble on guns that can't find targets.
349: Built around Gladiator Lancers, Thunderwolf Cavalry, and Vindicators backed by Jump Pack Assault Intercessors and Wolf Guard Terminators, this is the Stormlance Task Force in its most literal form — a hard-riding mixed-arms force that refuses to commit to a single threat axis. The plan is to use Thunderwolves and Jump Intercessors to force early melee commitments while Gladiator Lancers and Vindicators punish anything that repositions to avoid them, scoring primary through sustained mid-board presence rather than a single explosive turn. It punishes slower mid-range brawlers and planted gunlines that can't handle simultaneous melee and armoured pressure from multiple angles — the Thunderwolf charge threat alone forces bad positioning decisions from T5-6 infantry hordes. The weakness is the same multi-axis identity that makes it flexible: without a dominant damage engine, concentrated anti-armour fire from Knights or mobile shooting from Drukhari/Aeldari skimmer lists picks apart each threat in isolation before they can converge.
334: Built around three or more Redemptor Dreadnoughts supported by a Techmarine's repair aura and anchored by either Roboute Guilliman or Marneus Calgar in the Armour of Antilochus, this is an Anvil Siege Force or Ironstorm Spearhead expression centered on T9 walkers as the primary damage and scoring chassis. The engine is Techmarine-sustained Redemptors camping mid-board objectives — the Macro Plasma Incinerator and Onslaught Gatling Cannon profiles put AP-3 and AP-2 fire into anything from T5 infantry to T9 vehicles, while Guilliman's reroll aura and the Lieutenant's buff stack lift average wound output to the point where the list wins the firepower trade over turns two through four. It punishes static heavy gunlines and durable T7-9 vehicle lists that lack the speed to escape sustained AP-3+ concentrated fire, and the Techmarine's heal loop means opponents need two full rounds of focus fire to clear a single Redemptor rather than one. Fast kiting lists like Drukhari Realspace Raiders or Reaper's Wager crack it open by denying the firing solution entirely — Redemptors at 8" movement can't catch a 14-16" Raider, and the list's secondary-scoring reach collapses when the opponent refuses the mid-board engagement.
332: Built around Vulkan He'stan and Adrax Agatone stacking Salamanders flame-and-melta synergies, delivered via Land Raider Redeemer with Infernus Squads and Eradicators providing the ranged punch — this is a Forgefather's Seekers list where every weapon profile benefits from He'stan's re-rolls to wound against vehicles and Agatone's Strength buff on flame weapons. The engine is a two-track kill chain: the Land Raider Redeemer disgorges Infernus Squads or Bladeguard into contested mid-board while Eradicators at 24" spike AP-4 Melta into whatever armoured target needs to die that turn, with He'stan's aura converting wound rolls of 1 into genuine damage across both fire lanes. It punishes static vehicle-heavy or transport-infantry lists that cluster chassis together, because Melta 2D6-pick-highest inside 12" combined with flame overwatch from Infernus Squads makes any trade into this list catastrophically expensive in wound potential. Mobile skimmer lists and fast melee toolboxes crack it open by dictating engagement range — once a Drukhari Raider or a Cursed Legion Skorpekh unit forces the Land Raider to react rather than deliver, the crit-stacking kill chain collapses at 40.6% efficiency and never recovers.
333:
Built around Kayvaan Shrike and Aethon Shaan leading Vanguard Veterans and Assault Intercessors with jump packs alongside Centurion Devastators and Inceptors, this is a Vanguard Spearhead list that pairs mobile melee strikers with a planted heavy-fire base — Shrike's infiltrate and -1 to hit aura screening the Centurions while jump infantry hunt exposed characters via Precision.

The engine scores by threatening every zone simultaneously: Centurion Devastators anchor mid-board and delete elite targets with AP-3+ heavy bolters and lascannons, while Shrike-led jump assault units deepstrike or infiltrate to pin opposing scoring pieces and deny secondary runs, winning primary on tempo.

The mixed threat vectors punish static gunlines and low-mobility durable lists that can't spread their anti-vehicle fire across both the heavy-fire base and the incoming jump infantry wave.

The 41% win rate signals a list that struggles against fast anti-armour pressure — Mont'ka JSJ suits and Chaos Knights Infernal Lance crack the Centurion base before the melee strikers can neutralize the threat, and once the heavy-fire anchor is gone the list loses its damage ceiling.
348: Built around Ragnar Blackmane and Wolf Guard Battle Leaders leading Blood Claws and Wolf Guard Headtakers, this is a Champions of Russ melee-rush list that floods mid-board with high-volume, low-cost Assault infantry backed by Wolf Scouts for flanking pressure and a Ballistus Dreadnought as the long-range anchor. The plan is to use Ragnar's reroll-charge aura and Wolf Guard character stacking to deliver Blood Claws into melee on turn 2 while Wolf Scouts deny backfield objectives and the Ballistus picks off exposed support units, grinding primary through sheer body count and activation volume. It punishes static gunlines and transport-heavy lists that can't screen every approach — Blood Claws threatening multiple charge vectors forces opponents to either spread their anti-infantry firepower thin or cede midfield objectives entirely. The win rate signals a genuinely struggling build: layered-defense lists like Custodes Talons (2+/4++ absorbing the charge) and Death Guard Vectorium (Disgustingly Resilient shrugging off AP-1 chip damage) wall it out, and the lack of dedicated anti-armour beyond the single Ballistus means T9+ chassis sit comfortably outside the kill range of Blood Claws regardless of how many attacks they throw.
347: Built around Wulfen with storm shields, Thunderwolf Cavalry, and Wolf Guard Terminators delivered behind a Scout screen, Wolf Jail is the Stormlance Task Force's defining expression — a 4+/5++ melee brick with genuine multi-threat charging pressure. The engine is controlling mid-board engagement: Scouts deny deep strike corridors and force the opponent into unfavorable positioning while Thunderwolves and Wulfen threaten simultaneous charges from multiple angles, scoring primary through displacement and objective lockdown rather than incremental chip damage. Its layered 4+ invulnerable saves across Wulfen and Wolf Guard Terminators laugh at AP-1/AP-2 volume fire from Mobile Anti-Armour and skimmer-chassis lists that can't concentrate enough AP-3+ to clear the brick before it connects. Static gunlines and Heavy Gunline Toolbox lists that can't reposition after the Thunderwolves close 12" in a single activation are the natural prey — but lists with sufficient Lethal Hits density and FNP stacking, like Death Guard Vectorium, grind back efficiently through Disgustingly Resilient, turning the trade economy against the Wolves' relatively low model count.
274: Built around Commander in Coldstar, Crisis Sunforge, Starscythe, and Fireknife Battlesuits in a Mont'ka Jump-Shoot-Jump frame, this is T'au's premier mobile anti-armour expression — a Crisis-Commander stack that covers every threat profile across four distinct suit loadouts. The win condition is JSJ repositioning: advance into Melta or AP-3+ range turn 1, spike a priority target with concentrated Sunforge Melta fire or Fireknife plasma, then bounce back outside retaliation range before the opponent activates — scoring primary through sheer board pressure as thinned opponents can't contest objectives. It punishes static gunlines and slow durable-grind lists ruthlessly, because AP-3+ Melta at 12" combined with Commander Farsight's re-roll aura concentrates enough damage to delete T9 chassis before they can return fire at range. Its weakness is volume infantry and activation-gap armies — War Horde or Pactbound Zealots lists with 12-15 activations simply outnumber the suit stack on objectives, and once Cultist screens or Boyz mobs lock a Battlesuit in melee, the JSJ engine stalls entirely.
273: Built around Riptide Battlesuits, Hammerhead Gunships, and Piranhas backed by Pathfinder and Stealth Battlesuit screening, this is the Experimental Prototype Cadre in its most weapon-diverse expression — heavy rail and ion firepower on fast chassis, not the Mont'ka JSJ beatdown. The engine is Pathfinder-spotlight-into-Riptide-delete: Markerlights strip cover and boost BS, then Riptides with Heavy Burst Cannons or Ion Accelerators spike damage onto priority targets while Hammerheads handle armoured chassis at AP-3+ range, and Piranhas plus Stealthsuits screen the shooting base and contest secondaries. It punishes static gunlines and slow-moving elite armies that can't dictate range — the combined 14-18" movement across the roster forces opponents to either advance into Markerlight-buffed firing lanes or concede primary ground. Fast melee delivery threatens to crack it open: War Horde Boyz mobs or Pactbound Zealots with Rhino-rush delivery can close the 24" buffer before the Riptide fires twice, and without enough bodies to screen every angle, a single committed melee wave can dismantle the entire shooting platform.
276: Breacher Teams in Devilfish, backed by Cadre Fireblades, Sky Ray Gunships, and Hammerhead Gunships, this is Mont'ka in its purest competitive form — fast mechanised infantry delivering close-range pulse fire while vehicle platforms handle the anti-armour workload. The engine is Jump-Shoot-Jump repositioning: Devilfish advance Breachers into rapid-fire range for Cadre Fireblade-boosted S5 volume, Sky Rays lock down enemy flyers and strip overwatch, and Hammerheads spike T9+ chassis with AP-3 railgun fire before repositioning out of retaliation arcs. It punishes static gunlines and low-mobility vehicle lists brutally — anything that can't match the JSJ tempo gets picked apart piecemeal while the Tau score primary unopposed. Aggressive melee delivery and mass-body Transport Infantry lists crack it open, as Breacher squads exposed mid-board are fragile once the Devilfish hull is popped, and activation-dense screens prevent the clean fire-and-fade the list depends on.
275:
Built around Krootox Rampagers, Krootox Riders, and Kroot Lone-Spears as the damage backbone, supported by Kroot Hounds and Carnivore blobs, this is the Auxiliary Cadre's all-Kroot hunting pack — a melee-forward swarm that hits harder than it looks on a T3-4 chassis.

The engine is board saturation: Carnivore and Farstalker screens absorb pressure while Krootox Rampagers and Lone-Spears threaten T7-9 chassis in melee with high-volume Devastating Wounds attacks, closing distance via advance moves and native speed before the opponent can isolate and delete the damage dealers.

Against static Heavy Gunline lists, the combination of screening bodies, high activation count, and fast melee reach lets it close 24" before Russ blast templates fully clear the mobs — the Rampagers hit vehicles hard enough that even a reduced mob threatens vehicle hull points on the charge.

Mobile Anti-Armour Vehicle lists punish it hardest: Knight chassis with 12"+ movement and AP-3 Melta can strip Krootox Rampagers at range before they engage, and T3 wound pools evaporate quickly without a reliable invulnerable save to absorb the focused fire.
357: Built around Genestealers led by a Broodlord, supported by Neurolictor, Von Ryan's Leapers, and Lictors screening the advance, this is the Assimilation Swarm's purest expression — a wall of rending claws delivered through infiltrate and deepstrike rather than transports. The engine is Broodlord-buffed Genestealer charges from unexpected angles: Neurolictor and Lictors suppress Overwatch and strip defensive strats while Leapers and Gargoyles flood forward to deny screens and force early combats, letting the Genestealer bricks crash in with full re-rolls and Lethal Hits on 5+. It punishes planted gunlines and slow durable lists that can't reposition — once the infiltrate-and-deepstrike wave is in their deployment zone, Heavy Gunline Toolbox lists in particular run out of safe firing arcs and get locked in melee before their Blast weapons matter. Mobile Anti-Armour vehicles and Transport Infantry counter it hard, as AP-3+ melta concentration pops the T4 Genestealer bricks in a single activation before the Broodlord buffs ever resolve.
277: Built around Broadsides as the primary damage engine, supported by Ghostkeel and Stealth Battlesuit screens, Shadowsun's command aura, and Kroot Hounds absorbing early charges, this is a Kauyon-flavored static gunline that floods the board with AP-3+ heavy rail and missile fire from multiple T5-6 chassis simultaneously. The plan is to hold a deep firing line, force the opponent to advance into concentrated Broadside volleys across turns 2-3, and outscore on primary while the shooting steadily collapses the opponent's key units. It punishes low-model-count anti-armour and melee-delivery lists hardest — Knights and CSM Rhino-rush both bleed activations trying to close 24"+ under sustained AP-3 Railgun and Smart Missile System fire before the trade becomes favorable. The critical vulnerability is fast objective-flooding armies: a Subterranean Assault deepstrike or Pactbound screen-and-advance can swamp the Kroot hound buffer and lock Broadsides in melee, where their T5 2+ save stops mattering and their zero-fallback shooting profile collapses scoring entirely.
365: Built around the Mutalith Vortex Beast, Exalted Sorcerers, and dense Rubric Marine squads supported by an Infernal Master and Forgefiend, Warpforged Cabal is Thousand Sons playing a surprisingly grounded Transport Infantry game — psyker-blessed infantry pushing forward in numbers, not the fragile glass-cannon psychic castle the faction is stereotyped as. The engine is Rubric Marine bodies claiming and sticking objectives while the Mutalith's aura debuffs enemy saves and the Exalted Sorcerers stack Dark Pact crits and Infernal Fusillade spikes to clear contesting units. The broad playstyle spread — Transport Infantry, Mass Horde, and Mid-T Brawler all running high — means it punishes lists that lack the anti-infantry volume to clear T4 3+/5++ Rubrics efficiently, especially static gunlines that can't redirect fire once the Forgefiend and Mutalith are dictating threat angles. That same spread is the weakness: sitting near 49% win rate with no dominant axis means a focused counter — massed AP-2 or Lethal Hits volume stripping Rubric saves and FNP before the psyker engine comes online — unravels the list before it can compound its scoring.
363: Built around Sorcerers saturating Rubric Marines and Tzaangors with psychic buffs, a Daemon Prince of Tzeentch with Wings as the mobile hammer, and Magnus the Red as the list's apex threat, Cult of Magic is the premier Thousand Sons competitive detachment — a transport-and-body-count list dressed in robes and sorcery. The engine is Rubric Marines delivered forward in Rhinos or on foot behind Tzaangor screens, farming primary with bodies that ignore Morale and benefit from stacked psychic buffs, while Magnus and the Daemon Prince threaten flanks and characters with Lethal Hits-enabled melee and high-AP smite volume. Its mix of durable OC-generating battleline, activation depth from Tzaangor chaff, and concentrated burst threats punishes Heavy Gunline Toolbox and Transport Infantry lists that can't efficiently clear multiple 5+ invuln, FNP-equivalent infantry blobs across 3-5 objectives simultaneously. Fast mobile anti-armour and Mobile Anti-Armour pressure expose its core weakness — concentrated AP-3+ and Melta fire can strip the Rubric delivery vehicles and isolate Magnus before he engages, leaving the list's scoring engine walking forward into a firing line it was never built to survive.
364: Built around Scarab Occult Terminators led by a Sorcerer in Terminator Armour, Ahriman, a Daemon Prince of Tzeentch, and Tzaangor Enlightened as objective-flooding support, this is a Cult of Magic-style deep-strike hammer that uses the Terminators' 2+/4++ chassis as the durable delivery vehicle for massed Inferno Bolter and Force-weapon melee pressure. The engine fires by teleporting Scarab Occult blobs into mid-board on turns 1–2, using Ahriman's psychic amplification and Sorcerer stratagems to spike Lethal Hits on the Inferno Boltgun payload, while Sekhetar Robots and Tzaangor Enlightened flood secondaries from every table edge simultaneously. It punishes static defensive lists — Heavy Gunlines and AM Grizzled Company specifically — because the 2+/4++ profile eats Blast templates and Russ fire efficiently, and the volume of bodies contesting every objective makes primary-score denial nearly impossible. Concentrated AP-3+ anti-armour focus-fire from Mobile Anti-Armour lists (Infernal Lance Knight chassis, Mont'ka melta suits) is the crack — Melta rounds strip the 4++ through sheer volume of high-damage attacks before the Terminators can clear the threatening unit.
356: Built around Raveners, Hyperadapted Raveners, and Trygons burrowing up from reserves, with Swarmlord and Neurolictor providing command-and-control and Zoanthropes delivering psychic weight, this is the Tyranid Subterranean Assault detachment at its most tunneling-focused. The engine is Turn 1 and Turn 2 reserve drops: Trygons open holes for Ravener broods to surge onto mid-board objectives, while Swarmlord's command rerolls and Neurolictor's debuff auras isolate priority targets for the charge, scoring primary through sustained melee presence that most opponents can't efficiently clear. Its layered T5-6 bodies with 4+ invuln equivalents on Zoanthropes and decent wound pools punish static Heavy Gunline lists that can't reposition away from the underground threat or clear burrowing units fast enough before primary bleeds. However, Pactbound Zealots and similar Transport Infantry lists that screen with Cultist bodies and spike back with Devastating Wounds simply absorb the deepstrike and out-score on time, while Death Guard Vectorium's Disgustingly Resilient stacking and sticky objectives grind the charge momentum to nothing.
358: Built around Tervigon-spawned Termagant blobs screened by Venomthropes and anchored by Tyrant Guard, this is a mass-body Invasion Fleet list that buries the table in cheap OC and regenerating bodies. The engine is Tervigon replenishment: Termagant units that take casualties get topped back up, sustaining OC dominance across three to five objectives while Psychophages and Ripper Swarms deny deepstrike corridors and contest flanks. It punishes Heavy Gunline and static mid-range lists that can't generate enough activations to clear blobs faster than the Tervigon restocks them, especially when Venomthrope shroud saves force opponents to commit dedicated anti-infantry weight just to shift a single squad. It falls apart against AP-2 blast-template heavy lists and fast melee threats like Pactbound Zealots or Berzerker Warband that can chain-charge through the screen before the replenishment cycle stabilizes the front line — at a 42% win rate, the list is grinding uphill against the current meta's damage ceiling.
371: Built around Helbrutes as mobile anti-armour hammers, Masters of Executions as precision character-killers, and Khorne Berzerkers delivered via Chaos Land Raiders and Rhinos, this is a Vessels of Wrath-adjacent transport-rush list that leans harder into Helbrute firepower than the canonical Eightbound spine. The engine is transport delivery: Land Raiders disgorge Berzerkers onto contested objectives while Helbrutes threaten T7-9 chassis with their melta and fist profiles, and Jakhals screen the advance to deny early counter-charges and soak overwatch. It punishes static Heavy Gunline lists — Russ companies and planted fire-bases can't fall back from Berzerker charges and lack the activation count to clear both the Jakhal screen and the incoming transports in a single turn. However, it struggles against durable layered lists like Custodes Talons or Death Guard Vectorium, where the Helbrute's mid-AP melee output fails to efficiently clear 2+/4++ or FNP-stacked models before the trade goes negative.
370: Built around Forgefiend fire support, Eightbound and Exalted Eightbound as the elite melee hammers, Chaos Spawn as expendable screens, and Jakhals holding flanks, this is the Berzerker Warband detachment running a hybrid ranged-and-melee toolbox rather than the pure Berzerker-rush most players expect. The engine is turn-2 delivery: Apoplectic Frenzy and Berzerker's Wrath strats spike the Eightbound and Slaughterbound into isolated targets while the Forgefiend's autocannons strip screens, converting a positional advantage into a primary-scoring lead that a depleted opponent can't recover. The 4+ invuln on Eightbound and Fight-on-Death from the Mark of Khorne stack punish elite melee lists that try to trade into the hammers, making dedicated Layered Lethal Combat grinds pay double for every engagement. At sub-50% win rate, the list bleeds badly into volume-infantry matchups — Pactbound Zealots and similar Transport Infantry shells screen the deepstrike threat with disposable bodies and outpace the Khornate engine on primary scoring before it can close.
355: Built around Exocrines, Maleceptors, Norn Emissaries, and Tyrannofexes backed by a Hive Tyrant and Lictors, this is Crusher Stampede's signature monster-spam roster — T9-12 chassis across every slot, each bringing a distinct damage profile. The engine is concentrated heavy-weapons fire from multiple high-Toughness platforms simultaneously: Exocrines output S7 Blast at 36" with Lethal Hits potential, Tyrannofexes crack vehicles with AP-2 shooting, and Maleceptors deliver mortal wounds in melee while the Hive Tyrant stacks Synapse buffs — Lictors handle character sniping and screen-bypass to clear the scoring path. Against static gunlines and mid-range shooting armies, the list thrives by presenting six or more T9+ bodies that require dedicated anti-tank answers every single turn, overloading AP-limited rosters that can't kill faster than the monsters advance and score primary. The critical weakness is concentrated AP-3+ Melta from fast platforms — Knight or Mont'ka lists can focus-fire one monster per activation and dismantle the roster before the scoring engine reaches full pressure, while the list's near-zero screen coverage leaves individual monsters exposed to alpha-strike deletion.
373: Built around Bloodletters, Flesh Hounds, Skarbrand, Bloodcrushers, and a Bloodthirster with Forgefiend fire support, this is a Vessels of Wrath-adjacent Khorne Daemonkin shell that floods the board with Daemon keyword bodies across multiple distinct threat profiles. The engine is wave attrition: Flesh Hounds screen and threaten turn-1 charges while Bloodletters blob objectives, then Skarbrand and Bloodcrushers funnel into isolated targets where their Lethal Hits melee output and Fight on Death triggers compound the damage; the Forgefiend provides the only meaningful ranged threat to keep opponents honest. It punishes static gunlines and low-model-count anti-armour lists that can't efficiently clear multiple T4-5 Daemon waves across a wide frontage, especially since Bloodletter volume and Flesh Hound speed deny clean firing arcs before the big Daemons arrive. The list struggles badly into Transport Infantry shells like Pactbound Zealots, where Cultist screens absorb the deepstrike threat and crit-stacked Devastating Wounds shooting picks apart the Bloodthirster and Skarbrand before they can connect — and with no invulnerable saves heavier than a 5++, concentrated AP-2 or AP-3 fire from any gunline simply bleeds the horde faster than it can replace models.
372: Built around a Lord on Juggernaut leading Khârn, Khorne Berzerkers packed into Chaos Rhinos, Exalted Eightbound as the elite hammer, and Jakhals plus Chaos Spawn absorbing return fire, this is the Berzerker Warband at full tilt — a Khorne infantry-rush that uses transport delivery and character stacking to get the right threat into the right engagement every turn. The engine is crit-stacking via Pactbound-adjacent Dark Pact triggers and Apoplectic Frenzy burst windows: Berzerkers disembark and spike damage through Devastating Wounds crits while the Lord on Juggernaut's 14" threat range forces your opponent to either spread to contest objectives or clump and eat the full charge. It punishes static gunlines and mid-board objective holders hard — Rhino delivery compresses the distance before firing arcs can dictate the trade, and the Mark of Khorne Fight-on-Death chain means clearing a Berzerker squad costs the opponent more than the squad is worth. It struggles against high-body Transport Infantry mirrors and anything with layered defensive stacking — a Plague Marine screen backed by Plagueburst Crawlers soaks the charge through Disgustingly Resilient and Contagion debuffs, while the list's low model count bleeds primary scoring against any opponent who simply has more bodies on the table.
